issue_title: Solve the 'inline' consternation
description:
The [definition of JITINLINE]( as well potentially other places in the code, causes consternation. Specifically, if you compile C files with newer C compilers, JITINLINE doesn't emit a symbol, causing compilation failures such as ../tr.source/trj9/runtime/MethodMetaData.h:366:18: error: inline function ‘getByteCodeInfoFromStackMap’ declared but never defined [-Werror]
This has been worked around previously by forcing newer C compilers to use the old standard, but this really should be resolved once and for all, and likely, across the whole codebase.

issue_title: document tr.jit options
description:
It would be worthwhile to document the hidden treasures of trjjit optimizations (a significant portion of j9options.cpp) for:
- Users to gain insight into the (so far) under-documented tr jit features, take advantage of it by applying fine grained compiler customizations based on the specific environment and workload.
- Community members to better acquiant with the optimizations, hack around with the code with ease, get upto speed for large scale collaboration.

issue_title: Strange performance issues with OpenJ9 in this jmh bench...
description:
[I'm creating a jmh version of the benchmarks]( of [The computer language benchmarks game]( and I decided to try it out comparing OpenJ9 to Zulu9 from azul. Zulu9's performance is around 2600ms/op on my system, but OpenJ9 shows some strange performance issues where it slows down with every successive warmup iteration:
Zulu9 - sbt "jmh:run -i 10 -wi 20 -f1 -t1 -r 15 -jvmusr/lib/jvm/zulu-9/bin/java"
[info] # Run progress: 0.00% complete, ETA [info] # Fork: 1 of 1

[info] # Warmup Iteration 5: 2504.948 ms/op
[info] # Warmup Iteration 6: 2566.648 ms/op
[info] # Warmup Iteration 7: 2537.053 ms/op
[info] # Warmup Iteration 8: 2500.211 ms/op
[info] # Warmup Iteration 9: 2576.959 ms/op
[info] # Warmup Iteration 10: 2517.836 ms/op
[info] # Warmup Iteration 11: 2514.588 ms/op
[info] # Warmup Iteration 12: 2508.471 ms/op

[info] # Warmup Iteration 14: 2529.385 ms/op
[info] # Warmup Iteration 15: 2508.744 ms/op

OpenJ9 - sbt "jmh:run -i 10 -wi 20 -f1 -t1 -r 15 -jvmhome/mhammons/jdk-9+181/bin/java"
[info] # Run progress: 0.00% complete, ETA [info] # Fork: 1 of 1
[info] # Warmup Iteration 1: 36902.857 ms/op
[info] # Warmup Iteration 2: 41640.554 ms/op
[info] # Warmup Iteration 3: 49802.187 ms/op
[info] # Warmup Iteration 4: 59686.587 ms/op
[info] # Warmup Iteration 5: 69178.086 ms/op
[info] # Warmup Iteration 6: 78664.955 ms/op
...
As you can see, OpenJ9 starts off markedly slower than Zulu9. But what's more concerning is that instead of improving in performance during the warmup phase as is to be expected, the subsequent warmup iterations grow slower and slower on OpenJ9.
The benches were compiled with openjdk 8, and run with a forked jvm by the jmh harness. You can invoke the benches and indicate the jvm to be used to run them with the following command:
sbt "jmh:run -i 10 -wi 20 -f1 -t1 -r 15 -jvm path/to/jvm"
JVM arguments can be supplied with an added -jvmArgs argument. I did this with -Xjit:verbose to test that jitting was occurring, and it was, so this slowdown is puzzling. Another thing I noted while running this bench is that although it is designed to use as much threading as the system's cpus will allow for, half or less of my cpu was unused with OpenJ9.

issue_title: PROPOSAL: Labeling schema for managing issues
description:
As this project grows, and the number of open issues being tracked grows, a common labeling schema will be helpful to manage the project's issues. Taking some of the best practices at other large open projects I propose the following
- defining an small initial set of reserved labels generally applicable to majority of issues
- defining a reserved label colour for each category of label, ie. Priority labels are Green, component labels are blue. This enables quick location of relevant labels.
- label text should start with the category, ie. not "Medium", but "Pri: Medium", or "Comp: VM" . Helps new people identify purpose quickly
- Reserve a red "HOT" or similar red label for drawing attention to Urgent issues.
For the initial set of labels to define ( beyond the Git Default set)
- Priority, - Component, - Type (bug vs. discussion vs enhancement vs question), - Size (fixed unitless values), - JDK Level (as a project that supports multiple JDK API levels, identifying when a issue is unique to only 1 level will be useful), - red "Hot" label, - Beginner label to identify easy to take on work for new contributors.
Beyond that initial set, individuals might create their own labels as they find them useful, but conflicting with the project's defined set/colours should be discouraged.

issue_title: Enable requesting PR builds with dependent changes (Jenkins)
description:
Related #91 #11 #24
 Background
By default, a PR build will pull the openj9 branches of the openj9-openjdk-jdk9 and the openj9-omr repos. Sometimes developers have changes in openj9 that depend on changes they are working on in one or both of the other repos. We therefore need a process to request PR builds which can checkout the PR(s) of the other repo(s).
- A dependent change must be at eclipse/omr, eclipse/openj9-omr or ibmruntimes/openj9-openjdk-jdk9
- A PR with the dependent change must be open at the appropriate repo
- A committer must be able to request an openj9 PR build with dependent changes by supplying the namespace, repo and PR number in the trigger phrase.
 Syntax
 Default
`Jenkins test sanity`
 Dependent change at OMR
`Jenkins test sanity depends eclipse/omr#<PR#>`
 Dependent change at OpenJDK
`Jenkins test sanity depends ibmruntimes/openj9-openjdk-jdk9#<PR#>`
 Dependent change at OMR and OpenJDK
`Jenkins test sanity depends eclipse/omr#<PR#> ibmruntimes/openj9-openjdk-jdk9#<PR#>`
The reason/benefit of supplying the org/repo#PR is that Github will automatically generate a link to the dependent PR in the comment.

issue_title: SunFlow benchmark: unusual sensitivity to gcpolicy
description:
The SunFlow benchmark performed poorly with the initial release of OpenJ9 (slower than HotSpot by a factor of about 5x). A large part of the problem was solved by the fix for (available in current downloads from AdoptOpenJDK), and/or by selecting a larger fixed size heap.
Testing on 32 core Xeon(R) CPU E7-8867
(time in seconds, smaller is better)
Initial release of OpenJ9: 5s HotSpot: 0.98s
fixed 3G heap OpenJ9: 1.4s
fixed 3G heap HotSpot: 0.92
3G heap, optthruput : 0.67
During the course of the testing we discovered that on some machines changing the gcpolicy had a significant impact on the reported test results while on other machines there was no measurable difference. On the machine used for the above results, setting -Xgcpolicy:optthruput in conjunction with a fixed 3G heap reduced the required time to process the image to 0.67s. It's not clear to me why the gcpolicy has such an impact in this case, as the time spent in gc is quite low, however we have seen a significant reduction in data cache misses with optthruput. Why gencon is incurring a high rate of data cache misses but optthruput is not is being investigated.
Testing on a four core i7-6820HQ machine showed OpenJ9 at equal performance to HotSpot at the 3G heap size, and without any measurable sensitivity to choice of gcpolicy.

issue_title: Separate binaries (libjvm.so, etc.) required for Java 18.3
description:
This issue was brought up during investigation of `Java 18.3` build against `openj9-openjdk-jdk18.3`.
Current `OpenJ9 Java 9` builds doesn't have `classlib.properties` file to specify vm shape value, and `J2SE_SHAPE_LATEST` is defined to latest VM shape `J2SE_SHAPE_B165`. However `Java 18.3` build requires a newer shape value `J2SE_SHAPE_B1803` for `J2SE_SHAPE_LATEST`.
Hence separated binaries are required to accommodate both `Java 9 & 18.3` builds. `JAVA_SPEC_VERSION` seems a good candidate flag to differentiate these Java builds.
fyi @DanHeidinga @pshipton @adamfarley

issue_title: Undesirable behaviours by overriding MAKEFLAGS in OpenJ9.gmk
description:
Following `OpenJ9.gmk` script overrides `MAKEFLAGS`
`
# openjdk makeflags don't work with openj9/omr native compiles; override with number of cpus which openj9 and omr need supplied
override MAKEFLAGS := -j $(JOBS)
`
This effectively overrides the command line options from makefile caller. For example, `Main.gmk` invokes `OpenJ9.gmk` with command line option `VERSION_MAJOR=$(VERSION_MAJOR)` which could be overridden by hard-coded setting `VERSION_MAJOR:=9` hence cause the problem described in and a workaround has to be introduced to avoid the overriding.

issue_title: Investigate making compressed references a runtime and not a compile time decision
description:
Currently the OpenJ9 VM can not support both compressed references and not compressed references for 64 bit JVMs at the same time. This means to create a JDK that supports both you need to have 2 JVMs which significantly increases the footprint of the JDK package, the complexity of creating the JDK and the time it takes to create the JDK.
I am creating this Issue to start the conversation about what needs to be completed to make compressed references a runtime decision such that the JVM supports both at the same time.
creator: charliegracie
labels: enhancement, comp:vm, comp:gc, comp:jit, comp:doc, comp:build

Bug Description: Currently the OpenJ9 VM can not support both compressed references and not compressed references for 64 bit JVMs at the same time. This means to create a JDK that supports both you need to have 2 JVMs which significantly increases the footprint of the JDK package, the complexity of creating the JDK and the time it takes to create the JDK.
I am creating this Issue to start the conversation about what needs to be completed to make compressed references a runtime decision such that the JVM supports both at the same time.

description:
Currently we can launch PR builds with dependent changes that are in an open PR at omr, openj9-omr or openj9-openjdk-jdk9. There is a use case to launch a PR build against a branch instead of an open PR. For example, when the dependent or breaking PR has been merged in OMR and can't promote through OMR-Acceptance.
More info on dependent changes
If we can temporarily survive without this feature, it would be nice to finish off #660, #851 first. Which will commit all the build code in.

issue_title: -Xinternalversion not working on Java 8 builds
description:
-Xinternalversion is an accepted option on Java 8 but it doesn't provide any information, showing `Eclipse OpenJ9 OpenJDK 64-bit Server VM () from -amd64 JRE (), built on Jan 11 2018 by with`.
Example of a working version from Java 9
`Eclipse OpenJ9 OpenJDK 64-bit Server VM (9-internal+0-adhoc.openj9.openjdk) from linux-amd64 JRE (9-internal+0-adhoc.openj9.openjdk), built on Jan 11 2018 by openj9 with g++ (Ubuntu 4.8.4-2ubuntu1~14.04.3) 4.8.4`
OpenJDK8 does support -Xinternalversion, i.e.
`OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM (25.71-b00) for linux-amd64 JRE (1.8.0-internal-arnold_2017_11_27_12_41-b00), built on Nov 27 2017 by "arnold" with gcc 4.8.5 20150623 (Red Hat 4.8.5-4)`
The implementation uses a number of defines (J9PRODUCT_NAME, J9PRODUCT_NAME, J9PRODUCT_NAME, etc) which are expected to be defined in openj9_version_info.h, but something isn't working in the Java 8 build process. The process was copied from the Java 9 build ,where it works. The file is defined here and scripting in overlays the file on the OpenJ9 source.
It seems a number of the configure variables which are used for Java 9 don't exist in Java 8.
 COMPILER_VERSION_STRING
 HOTSPOT_TARGET_OS -> OPENJDK_TARGET_OS
 USERNAME -> only USER_RELEASE_SUFFIX which looks like `peter_2017_09_28_16_31`
 VERSION_STRING -> JRE_RELEASE_VERSION

issue_title: Jenkins log and artifact cleanup schedule
description:
Today we took down Eclipse's [hipp5]( which is where our OpenJ9 Jenkins master lives. We were consuming 264G space according to the [Bugzilla]( and have been asked to reduce.
What we store:
- Build logs (console output)
- SDKs from Builds and PRs
Jenkins has the following options, which are configured on a per job basis
Days to keep builds, if not empty, build records are only kept up to this number of days Max # of builds to keep, if not empty, only up to this number of build records are kept Days to keep artifacts, if not empty, artifacts from builds older than this number of days will be deleted, but the logs, history, reports, etc for the build will be kept Max # of builds to keep with artifacts, if not empty, only up to this number of builds have their artifacts retained
Currently, our nightly (and OMR acceptance) builds are setup with the following:
- Days to keep builds: 60
- Max # of builds to keep: 100
- Days to keep artifacts:
- Max # of builds to keep with artifacts: 10
Our PR builds are not configured to discard (keep everything).
 Propose:
Nightlies and OMR Acceptance:
- Days to keep builds: 60
- Max # of builds to keep: 100
- Days to keep artifacts: ~7~
- Max # of builds to keep with artifacts: ~10~
PRs:
- Days to keep builds: 60
- Max # of builds to keep: 100
- Days to keep artifacts: ~14~
- Max # of builds to keep with artifacts: ~25~
Please review @pshipton Also, I have a script to check disk space I could add a job for and send a Slack notification if we're over X. Could open as a separate issue if we're interested.

issue_title: Format of the version for Eclipse OpenJ9
description:
Eclipse OpenJ9 is soon to create a 0.8 release. It makes sense to expose this version from Java at runtime. The appropriate place is the java.vm.version system property (which is currently 2.9 as inherited from IBM). The current proposal is to set java.vm.version to the tag used for the build, which for the next OpenJ9 release will be openj9-0.8 or openj9-0.8.0. This Issue is for discussion.
The java.vm.version affects the java -version output, as seen below on the "Eclipse OpenJ9 VM" line where
the following example shows "build openj9-0.8.0". openjdk version "1.8.0_152"
OpenJDK Runtime Environment (build 1.8.0_152-b16)
Eclipse OpenJ9 VM (build openj9-0.8.0, JRE 1.8.0 Linux amd64-64 Compressed References 20180130_000000 (JIT enabled, AOT enabled)
OpenJ9 - 296975c3
OMR - f410d656
JCL - 687ce89fd9 based on jdk8u152-b16)
For un-tagged (non-release) builds, the java.vm.version would be `<branch>-<sha>`, i.e. `master-a3814e1`.
Note OpenJ9 is still an incubation project. The Eclipse Project Handbook contains the following guidance. Perhaps the java.vm.version should indicate the incubation status of the project.
"In order to alert potential consumers of the incubating nature, projects in the incubation phase must include incubation branding. The project team must:
- Display the incubation logo on their project web page (if they have one);
- Display the incubation logo on their project’s primary download page;
- Include the word "incubation" in the filename of all downloadable files (when technically feasible) for builds and milestones; and
- When technically feasible, include the word "incubation" in features (e.g. about dialogs, feature lists, and installers)."
@mstoodle @DanHeidinga

issue_title: Inconsistent case-sensitivity in Xtrace
description:
The destination and trigger Xtrace clauses behave differently with regard to case-sensitivity. For example, the print option doesn't care about case, so both of these options work:
` -Xtrace:print=j9thr.0`
` -Xtrace:print=J9THR.0`
However, trigger clauses _do_ care about case, so this option works:
` -Xtrace:trigger=tpnid{j9thr.0,javadump}`
but this option doesn't:
` -Xtrace:trigger=tpnid{J9THR.0,javadump}`
 To make things worse, you can't just make a mental note to always specify tracepoint IDs in lower case because different tracepoint IDs can use different cases - e.g. OpenJ9 tracepoints are in lower case, but IBM JCL tracepoints are in uppercase.
I think the best solution is to remove case-sensitivity for trigger clauses.

issue_title: ConstantDynamic: Resolving Constant_Dynamic entries
description:
LDC bytecode

The ldc bytecode will have to be modified to detect Condy constants. If the constant or exception doesn’t exist in the ramConstantPool attempt to resolve the constant. If the exception exists throw the exception (Note: if LDC of Condy causes an exception, the same exception must be thrown every time). If the constant exists return the constant.

LDC2lw bytecode

The ldc2_w byte will check the cp type via something like `J9_CP_TYPE(cpShapeDescription, cpIndex)`. If it is not a Condy entry normal execution will occur. If it is, romConstantPool entry will be NULL check for the Condy constant, then for the exception. If both are NULL then resolution will occur. When the constant is resolved the long or double will be extracted from the object with something like `J9VMJAVALANGLONG_VALUE` and then placed on the stack.

Resolving native side

Create a new helper in resovleSupport to resolve Condy CPentries. This can share a common helper with `resolveInvokeDynamic` as much of the functionality will be the same. In the case of Condy, the helper will need to fetch the `nameAndSig` and `bsmIndex` from the romCP entry. Otherwise, the rest of the calculations required to determine the start `bsmData` are the same as with Indy The helper will call `sendResolveConstantDynamic` (new function) to retrieve and run the BSM for the LDC. After the result will be cached in the ramConstantPool it is Condy. In the Condy case the helper will check if an exception was thrown upon returning from `sendResolveConsntantDynamic`. If an exception exists, it will be stored in the exception slot in the ramConstantPool entry. `sendResolveConstantDynamic` will be similar to `sendResolveInvokeDynamic`, it will perform a java call-in to `MethodHandle.resolveConstantDynamic()`

Resolving Java side

A new function `MethodHandle.resolveConstantDynamic()` will need to be added, this can share a common helper with `MethodHandle.resolveInvokeDynamic` as much of the code is the same. A boolean can be added the helper args to identify whether it is resolving for Condy or Indy. If Condy is detected the third parameter to the `staticArgs` array with be a Class instead of a MethodType. A new entry will have to be added for Condy when marshalling the args. And a new native will have to be added to `java_dyn_methodhandle.c` to retrieve the a CondyConstant (to start we can avoid putting Condy constants in args until the native is implemented #1276). If resolving for Condy the invokeWithArgs stage will cast and return an Object rather than a Callsite. The result will be validated based on the steps specified in the spec and then returned. If an exception occurs the exception is thrown.

issue_title: Cleanup class scanning in Balanced
description:
J9 Class scanning in Balanced is initiated as soon as correspondent Class Object is discovered in the object heap. It calls a number of iterators to scan J9 scan class related parts:
 - GC_ClassStaticsIterator for RAM Statics
 - GC_CallSitesIterator for Call Sites
 - GC_ConstantPoolObjectSlotIterator for Constant Pool
 - GC_MethodTypesIterator twice for Method Types and Var Handle Method Types
This pattern is the same for all Balanced components (Copy Forward, Global Mark, Partial Mark, Card Scrabber, Write Once Compactor)
There is a general Class Slots Iterator available: GC_ClassIterator
It calls all iterators listed above one by one, so potentially it can be used in Balanced instead.
It should be possible because the handling of slots for all iterators is the same and scanning order is not important. However GC_ClassIterator requires slight modification: it returns slots from J9 Class structure itself so Class Object might be scanned twice. It might create problems. So we should add logic to GC_ClassIterator to prevent Class Object to be returned back.
By the way there is a potential problem with J9 Class scanning in Balanced: we never scan J9 Class structure itself so rely on fact that there is only one object reference in it and this is Class Object has been scanned before. Using of improved GC_ClassIterator should solve this potential problem automatically.

issue_title: [Nestmates] Support invokevirtual of private methods in other classes
description:
Prior to nestmates, `invokevirtual` of private methods only occurred in the same class and could be rewritten to `invokespecial` at ROMClass creation time.
With nestmates, other classes in the nest can `invokevirtual` private methods of their mates. This info isn't known until resolution when we can't modify the bytecode. Additionally, the ROMClass could be in sharedclasses and this might not be a valid change from one run to the next due to separate compilation.
OpenJ9 needs to find a way to adapt to this in RAM & ROM constantpools.

issue_title: Valhalla LWVT: Add new bytecodes defaultvalue and withfield
description:
Latest L-World proposal: Latest rough draft JVMS: # defaultvalue
The `defaultvalue` bytecode pushes a reference to an instance of a value class onto the stack, initialized to the class' default values.
Stack:
... -->
..., valueref
The initial implementation should operate in the same way that the `new` bytecode does -- the instance should be allocated on the heap and a reference should be placed on the stack. A later version could consider value type buffering, where new instances are instead allocated in a valuebuffer pointed to from the Java stack, and which disappears when the stack frame is popped.
The default value for a value class is currently considered to be the same as for POJOs. That is zero for all scalars and NULL for all references. # withfield
The `withfield` bytecode pushes a new reference to a value class instance with an updated instance field. Stack:
..., valueref, value -->
..., newvalueref
Note: This is **NOT** like `putfield`. An existing value type is not being updated. Rather, a new instance with an updated field is being created.
Again, the initial implementation should allocate new instances on the heap, and a later implementation should consider value type buffering.

issue_title: Jenkins: parse JOB_NAME to set SPEC and SDK_VERSION variables
description:
Currently, we have Pipeline files which are essentially copy/pasted several times per SPEC and SDK_VERSION. It has been proposed that we just have a "generic" file that takes parameters for these 2 values. The issue with using parameters is they can be changed "on-the-fly" and since we have different jobs for each SPEC and SDK_VERSION, we do not want these to change from build to build.
Since we have a standard naming convention for our job names, another idea would be to write a function that sets the SPEC and SDK_VERSION based on the Jenkins JOB_NAME. I have prototyped this feature and it appears to work in the pipeline build. I wanted to open an issue to discuss this approach more. What would the limitations of this be? I can see difficulty arising when trying to debug a build. For example, I currently have a debug copy of a build and the SPEC and SDK in the job name doesn't always match the build I'm testing (I often change the JenkinsFile that is loaded). The other thing is we would need to maintain 2 more variables in the variables file which would be arrays of SPECS and SDK_VERSIONS. We may be able reuse these new variable arrays in the Build-Test-All pipeline?
Note: There is also hardcoded TEST_TARGET in the PR pipelines but I think we should ignore that for now because the test story may be changing.

issue_title: Switch to using Adopt JenkinsFiles for Test
description:
Currently we have our own [JeknkinsFiles for Test]( purposes ([also here]( We should be pulling the Test Jenkins files from [AdoptOpenJDK/openjdk-tests]( This will benefit us by not having to maintain our own "copies"
This work will require some help and coordination form the test team so we can have a smooth transition.
This may cause us to break out our PR builds into several builds (just like the nightly flow). There are a few issues with this.
1. Moving the SDK around can be slow on some machines (#659)
1. GH-PR-Trigger plugin only works with "1-build". Currently the PR builds run compile & test in a single build/job. The top-level job would be responsible for communicating with GitHub. We could switch to using "Build Status Messages" (see [example]( instead of the simple "Test result one liner" (which is inaccurate #981).
also related #1409 #1779 #2037

issue_title: Use environment variables for compilers in DockerFile(s)
description:
Currently, symbolic links are used to set compilers in `buildenv/docker/jdk*/.../DockerFile`.
# Create links for c++,g++,cc,gcc
RUN ln -s g++ /usr/bin/c++ \
 && ln -s g4.8 /usr/bin/g++ \
 && ln -s gcc /usr/bin/cc \
 && ln -s gcc-4.8 /usr/bin/gcc
@keithc-ca recommended usage of environment variables instead of symbolic links.
ENV CC gcc-4.8
ENV CXX g4.8

issue_title: Windows j9jit29.dll needs MSVCP100.dll (for Java 8) as a prereq
description:
For Java 8, the Windows j9jit29.dll has msvcp100.dll as a prerequisite and is the only dll in the OpenJ9 VM with this requirement. Unlike msvcr100, the msvcp100 dll is not included in the OpenJDK / OpenJ9 build packaging. Its needed by the JIT for the following:
 49F ?max@?$numeric_limits@_K@std@@SA_KXZ
 251 ?_Orphan_all@_Container_base0@std@@QEAAXXZ
 9A ??1_Container_base12@std@@QEAA@XZ
 28E ?_Xout_of_range@std@@YAXPEBD@Z
 28C ?_Xlength_error@std@@YAXPEBD@Z
 252 ?_Orphan_all@_Container_base12@std@@QEAAXXZ
I expect its similar for newer versions of Java, except they need msvcp120.dll, which today is typically already installed on Windows boxes, but this may not be true in the future.

issue_title: Enable a form of -Xshareclasses by default
description:
A form of -Xshareclasses should be enabled by default in order to provide startup time and footprint advantages.
There are a number of factors to consider:
1. what classloaders should be shared by default? -Xshareclasses enables URLClassLoader *and potentially subclasses of URLClassLoader* for class sharing. As we saw in #1244, the subclasses don't necessarily work, resulting in the JVM failing to start. Restricting to the bootstrap loader would resolve this, as would restricting to the bootstrap loader plus the application and extension (or platform) loaders. Given the application code and extension (or platform) code may be different from multiple JVM invocations, sharing only the bootstrap loader would be the safest option. 1. what should the cache be called? The cache will be shared by every invocation of the JVM from the same user. The username should be part of the cache name, which it already is by default. The shared cache is automatically destroyed (when possible) and recreated when the "unique id" of the VM attaching to the cache is different from the "unique id" of the VM which created the cache. Using the "unique id" as the cache name will ensure that only identical builds of the JVM can shared the cache. (fyi #1645).
1. what happens to abandoned default caches? Abandoned either because the JVM was updated, or the user added an explicit -Xshareclasses option. They will consume disk space, or on z/OS shared memory. There is an `-Xshareclasses:expire=<time in minutes>` option which destroys caches that haven't been used in the number of minutes specified. The VM could automatically destroy any default caches it finds which are unused for some period of time.

issue_title: Create a Large Heap (noncompressedrefs) build
description:
OpenJ9 supports both compressedrefs and non-compressedrefs packages. Currently, the project only builds and tests the compressedrefs package.
This is a problem for anyone wanting a heap larger than ~57 gig and limits adoption of OpenJ9 for projects that need large heaps.
The long term solution is outlined in but we need a more immediate way to meet this need.
Proposal
* Create a "Large Heap" OpenJ9 package for the non-compressedrefs mode to support users that need > ~57 gig heaps. * Enable building this package on all platforms but make it optional.
* Due to machine limitations, enable this package for compile and test:
 * OpenJ9: pLinux or Windows (depending on machine availability)
 * Adopt: Enable on xLinux
* Support this for JDK8 and newer releases (JDK10+)
Next steps:
 * [x] Remove any hardcoded references to compressedrefs from OpenJ9 and Extensions makefiles
 * [x] Update redirector to generate reasonable messages pointing to the other package when using `-Xcompressedrefs`/`-Xnoncompressedrefs`
* [x] Update build pipelines here to build the non-compressed package #1884
* [x] Add it to the OMR promotion criteria #1886
* [x] Determine what level of testing here for the non-compressed package
* [x] Work with Adopt to get this package built / tested there as well
Related: I'm sure I've missed details here so committers please feel free to edit this to add details I've missed.

issue_title: Jenkins: Looming space issue on slaves
description:
The way our builds currently work, we try to cleanup as much as possible after a build but we generally leave the OpenJDK repo in the workspace to save clone time on the next build (`git clean -ffxd`). This applies to all Build* and PullRequest* jobs. For Test* jobs we do a full `cleanWs()` because we do not clone OpenJDK in these jobs. Leaving the OpenJDK repo behind consumes 1.0-2.5G per workspace. As we add more and more builds, these start to add up and space on a slave starts to become an issue.
For example, looking at one of the zLinux slaves
jenkins@LXEOJ901:~/jenkins-agent/workspace$ du -shc *
2.5G Build-JDK10-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs
1.6G Build-JDK8-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs
1.2G Build-JDK9-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs
2.5G PullRequest-Compile-JDK10-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs-OpenJDK10
1.1G PullRequest-Compile-JDK8-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs-OpenJ9
1.1G PullRequest-Compile-JDK8-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs-OpenJDK8
1.5G PullRequest-Compile-JDK9-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs-OpenJ9
1.2G PullRequest-Extended-JDK8-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs-OpenJ9
1.6G PullRequest-Extended-JDK9-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs-OpenJ9
2.5G PullRequest-Sanity-JDK10-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs-OpenJ9
1.2G PullRequest-Sanity-JDK8-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs-OpenJ9
1.9G PullRequest-Sanity-JDK8-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs-OpenJDK8
1.6G PullRequest-Sanity-JDK9-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs-OpenJ9
1.5G PullRequest-Sanity-JDK9-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs-OpenJDK9
400M Test-Sanity-Functional-JDK8-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs
205M Test-Sanity-JDK10-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs
358M Test-Sanity-System-JDK8-linux_ppc-64_cmprssptrs_le
728M Test-Sanity-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs
269M Test-Sanity_System-linux_390-64_cmprssptrs
24.8G total
Note: The Test* ones should be `0` but if the last build failed to finish then they can leave contents behind.
My proposal is to have a reference repo on the slave and use it to clone OpenJDK. This will allow us to completely clean any/all workspaces and still have fast clones. We would therefore only have 3 repos stored on disk rather than the current 14-21.
More info about reference repos: Git also has the ability to store many repos in one repo cache (reference repo). We could therefore clone all versions of OpenJDK we need into one folder (like `~/openjdk_cache`) and ref it during our [clone of OpenJDK](
The SCM step we use to clone OpenJDK has the option for specifying a reference repo if available
Path of the reference repo to use during clone
Specify a folder containing a repository that will be used by Git as a reference during clone operations.
This option will be ignored if the folder is not available on the master or slave where the clone is being executed.
The other thing that might solve this issue is if we change the PR builds to use the Build and Test jobs, then we would only have the 3 build jobs per machine and no PR workspaces, as mentioned in #1450 .

issue_title: Enable DDR support for AIX
description:
Ties into #378 There is work needed in OpenJ9 and [eclipse/omr]( order to bring up DDR on AIX 7.1 and up. Broadly, this work will consist of:
- [x] Changing makefiles in order to add the debug flags necessary for DDR on AIX and account for platform differences when building DDR on AIX
- [x] Fixing any issues with compiling the DDR code on AIX
- [x] DDR relies on libdwarf, however, AIX does not seem to have a supported library, and OMR's DDR does not use it. Instead OMR has its own parser. This parser needs to be fixed or replaced with libdwarf if we can compile it on AIX.
- [x] Enable DDR by default in the extensions repos.
ibmruntimes/openj9-openjdk-jdk8#223
ibmruntimes/openj9-openjdk-jdk11#76
ibmruntimes/openj9-openjdk-jdk#59
- [x] Enabling `-g` causes the AIX stackframe to be too large. Need an alternative approach to ensure good perf with DDR enabled. See #3248. Fixed by #3995
- [x] Enable DDR tests on AIX #3995

issue_title: Cleanup line in VM_Test build.xml not working as expected
description:
<target name="clean" depends="dist" description="clean up">
 <!-- Delete the ${build} directory trees -->
 <delete dir="${build}" />
 <delete dir="${data}/*.class" />
 <delete dir="${databin}" />
 </target>
Specifically:
`<delete dir="${data}/*.class" />`
I believe the intention of this line is to delete all the class files within the `data` directory. I think the syntax currently reads "Delete all directories named `*.class` in the `data` directory" (where *.class is the actual name of a directory).
Ant doc: I created a simple test case by hand and tried it on Windows and xLinux and it doesn't delete any *.class **files** in my directory.
Changing the syntax to the following removes the class files in my dir.
<delete>
 <fileset dir="${data}" includes="**/*.class"/>
</delete>

issue_title: Unclear use of  OMRSIG_SIGNAL / OMRSIG_SIGACTION
description: A number of places in the jvm ( eg [1]( [2]( [3]( among others ), we use the macros `OMRSIG_SIGNAL` / `OMRSIG_SIGACTION` These macros are conditionally defined in [`omrport.h`]( to expand to `omrsig_primary_signal` / `omr_primary_sigaction` if `OMRPORT_OMRSIG_SUPPORT` is defined, or `signal` / `sigaction` otherwise. The issue is that we only define `OMRPORT_OMRSIG_SUPPORT` [when compiling the port library]( Thus these other reference are actually just calling `signal`/`sigaction`. Is this the intended behaviour? If so, shouldn't we make it more clear by avoiding the use of the macros? If not, we should be defining `OMRPORT_OMRSIG_SUPPORT` globally, or [merging it with `OMR_OMRPORT`](
creator: dnakamura

issue_title: Refactor Jenkins Build files
description:
Currently, we have too much duplication between our top level Jenkins build files. We need to come up with a solution to refactor these so we can reduce or eliminate this repetitive code.
Files in question:
- [x] [Build](
- [ ] ~[Test]( (perhaps unnecessary as we move to Adopt's test files #1450)
- [x] [Nightly Pipelines](
- [ ] [PullRequests]( (compile, sanity, extended)
One proposal is to parse the build name to set the SPEC and SDK_VERISON. Prototyped in #1396 Another option is to pass the SPEC and SDK_VERSION as build parameters.
The Build* and PullRequest-Compile* files are now identical (except for an extra timeout). So we could at least eliminate all the PullRequest-Compile files. However this would be an exception to the current convention. A larger refactor may make this irrelevant.

issue_title: Increase default shared cache size for Java 8 64-bit
description:
#1930 #1164 increased the default shared cache size for Java 9 and later. We should consider doing the same for Java 8. Since Java 8 may be the more often used JVM, increasing the default in Java 8 should be beneficial, especially for those enabling -Xshareclasses without understanding that typically the default size needs to be increased. We can wait a little bit and see if any problems are discovered by the change to Java 9 and later.

issue_title: Signals not working properly for Apache Kafka
description:
How to reproduce the issue?
**Instructions:** - Step 1: Download the code
`tar -xzf kafka_2.11-1.1.0.tgz; cd kafka_2.11-1.1.0`
- Step 2: Start the server in a new shell or in background (`&`)
`bin/zookeeper-server-start.sh config/zookeeper.properties`
- Step 3: Start the Kafka server in a new shell or in background (`&`)
`bin/kafka-server-start.sh config/server.properties`
**Observations:** Kafka overwrites the default signal handlers for `SIGTERM`, `SIGHUP` and `SIGINT`: [related Kafka source code](
Kafka also adds a [shutdown hook](
**Issue:** When a signal is raised (`SIGTERM`, `SIGHUP` and `SIGINT`), the newly assigned signal handler is invoked in an infinite loop. Need to investigate this behavior further.

issue_title: Eclipse equinox launcher does not recognise OpenJ9 java 10 as modular VM
description:
Mirrored from: I notice that the Eclipse Photon launcher has a test isModularVM() function here:
which tests jvm.dll for PRODUCT_VERSION_KEY to check the product version >= 9
Using Windows Explorer to find jvm.dll, then properties > details shows Oracle Java 10 has product version = 10.0.1.0 and file version 10.0.1.0
OpenJ9 has product version R2.9, file version 2.9.0.54
I don't know whether the launcher looks in the compressrefs, j9vm or server directories.
I think the result is that the Eclipse launcher thinks OpenJ9 is not a modular VM and strips off vmargs such as --add-modules=ALL-SYSTEM
To test, change in eclipse.ini --add-modules=ALL-SYSTEM to --add-modules=BADALL-SYSTEM and try to start Eclipse Photon under Oracle Java 10, and under OpenJ9 Java 10.
The Oracle version won't start, the OpenJ9 will.
Who should change - the Eclipse launcher or the OpenJ9 product version? Is there a standard way to test a VM version without starting it? The release file in the JDK root directory has a MODULES= line and
JAVA_VERSION="10.0.1"
OpenJ9, Oracle and IBM JVMs and JREs seem to all have this file. Perhaps it would be better than checking jvm.dll, but does involving finding the root of the jdk/jre.
Also consider Linux.

issue_title: Ability to provide test image in addition to JDK/JRE packages
description:
Native tests need executables or shared libraries. To enable those tests test image need to be built and accessible. Comments from @pshipton "The executables are already created as part of the OpenJ9 build, but the OpenJ9.gmk [1] doesn't copy them into the sdk or jre images (which is correct). They should be copied into the test image.
There will be changes required to keep the test image around so it can be used for testing. Currently we only keep the sdk image.
To extend on this, the test libraries should also be extracted from the vm directory and put into the test image. This will require fixes to the tests so they can use the shared libraries found in the test image instead of getting them "for free" as part of the VM."

issue_title: Support test only PR builds
description: In the current setup, committers can launch PR builds with SDK complication and tests on each platform and against different java version. However, there are lots of cases where we only need run test builds to verify test change and SDK compilation is not needed. In order to be more efficient in terms of machine resource and build execution time, I think we should support test only PR builds, so committers can launch test only build with pre-existed/staged SDK (maybe from nightly build).
creator: llxia
text:

Bug Description: In the current setup, committers can launch PR builds with SDK complication and tests on each platform and against different java version. However, there are lots of cases where we only need run test builds to verify test change and SDK compilation is not needed. In order to be more efficient in terms of machine resource and build execution time, I think we should support test only PR builds, so committers can launch test only build with pre-existed/staged SDK (maybe from nightly build).

issue_title: Issue with prefixed native methods
description:
Reported on behalf of a user:
OpenJ9 does not always respect native method prefix set with JVMTI call SetNativeMethodPrefix.
We do the following:
1. Start SwingSet2.jar without a profiler agent.
2. Attach the profiler agent.
3. Perform some bytecode instrumentation of loaded classes, including
wrapping native methods. We call JVMTI's SetNativeMethodPrefix
"$$YJP$$" as a parameter.
4. Exit the application. The following exception is printed to console:
With JDK 10:
Exception in thread "Thread-7" java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: com/ibm/lang/management/internal/MemoryNotificationThreadShutdown.
$$YJP$$sendShutdownNotification()V
 at com.ibm.lang.management.internal.MemoryNotificationThreadShutdown.sendShutdownNotification(jdk.management@10.0.1/MemoryNotificationThreadShutdown.java)
 at com.ibm.lang.management.internal.MemoryNotificationThreadShutdown.run(jdk.management@10.0.1/MemoryNotificationThreadShutdown.java:49)
With JDK 8:
Exception in thread "Thread-10" java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: com/ibm/lang/management/internal/MemoryNotificationThreadShutdown.
$$YJP$$sendShutdownNotification()V
 at com.ibm.lang.management.internal.MemoryNotificationThreadShutdown.sendShutdownNotification(MemoryNotificationThreadShutdown.java)
 at com.ibm.lang.management.internal.MemoryNotificationThreadShutdown.run(MemoryNotificationThreadShutdown.java:49)
It seems that the JVM does not link the prefixed native method
$$YJP$$sendShutdownNotification() to the original native symbol for
sendShutdownNotification(). There is no error when the agent is loaded on start with -agentpath.

issue_title: Numa has been disabled in Balanced gc by default due to interleaveMemory change
description:
In past, NUMA(affinity) on balanced gc and NUMA memory interleaving on gencon gc are enabled by default. From Java 8Sr5 NUMA interleave memory has been turned off by default, it also disable NUMA(affinity) on balanced gc.
This issue would not affect AIX-PPC and windows platforms.
currently the user could add "-XX:+InterleaveMemory" option for a workaround.

issue_title: Java 9,10,11 slow to start on zLinux
description:
Java 9,10,11 are slow to start on zLinux.
This problem seems to be the cause of #2329.
The default -Xmx for Java 9 and later is 25% of the physical memory. Startup time varies, but on a zLinux machine with 64GB, startup time without specifying -Xmx can be a second or more. Explicitly set -Xmx512m and its much faster. The time varies from run to run, and OS to OS. Explicitly setting an -Xmx which is equivalent to the default may also speed up the startup time.
creator: pshipton
labels: prio:high, jdk9, jdk10, comp:vm, comp:gc, jdk11

issue_title: Rework getJimModules()
description:
getJimModules() loads and caches `java/lang/reflect/Module`. This is currently used only by JVMTI.
Per suggest using `enterVMFromJNI
J9Class *clazz = J9VM_J9CLASS_FROM_JCLASS(vmThread, jclassForModule);
jimModule = &clazz->classObject;
exitVMToJNI
`
Also create a macro `JCLASS_FROM_J9CLASS ` to do `(jclass)&someJ9Class->classObject`
creator: pdbain-ibm

issue_title: DDR support for new vTable shape
description:
When the J9Class vTable gets larger due to invokevirtual private support (#2434), certain DDR extensions will become incorrect.
In order to maintain compatibility with older cores, the changes will need to be versioned (algorithm version):
1) Old-style vTable

The new-style will automatically handle and changes in shape to the header, so it will not need to be updated each time we add to the header.

issue_title: JVMTI should ignore extra callbacks
description:
JVMTI SetEventCallbacks currently fails if the size of the input callback table exceeds the number of callbacks known to the JVM. This causes problems if a future (not yet supported) version of JVMTI with more callbacks is used by an agent.
New versions of JVMTI never change the numbering of existing callbacks, so the solution is to simply ignore any callbacks that exceed the known size.

issue_title: [Condy] Allow invokeWithArguments of varargs methods to absorb extra args into trailing array
description:
To relax length restrictions on bootstrap specifiers, the language which defines the invocation of bootstrap methods will be adjusted (with complete backward compatibility) to allow variable arity (ACC_VARARGS) bootstrap methods to absorb, into their trailing arguments, all remaining static arguments, even if there are 2^16-1 of them. (The class-file format already allows this, although there is no way to read over-long bootstrap argument lists.) For consistency, the invokeWithArguments methods of MethodHandle will also be expanded in this way, if the target method has variable arity. In this way the invocation of bootstrap methods can be specified in terms of the weakly typed methods invokeWithArguments and invoke, just as today it is specified in terms of invoke alone.
BSM invocation may need to be updated as well if there is an explicit check. Currently it uses invokeWithArguments().

issue_title: Java 11 interpreter sometimes skips type test for super invokespecial in interface method
description:
Super `invokespecial` requires that the receiver be an instance of the current class (i.e. the class containing the `invokespecial` bytecode instruction). When the current class is an interface, this is not guaranteed by bytecode verification. Instead, the `invokespecial` instruction dynamically checks that the receiver implements the current interface, and if not, it throws `IllegalAccessError`.
The attached [`BadSuperInInterface`]( should print `true`, `false`, `true`, and then throw `IllegalAccessError`. I get the correct result from OpenJ9 if it is built as Java 8, or if it is built as Java 11 and JIT options force the `nosey` method to be compiled. But if `nosey` is interpreted in Java 11, I don't get an exception.
The problem appears to have been introduced by #2434. If I build with that commit reverted, I get the exception again.
I tried to reduce the test case further with [`InterfaceInvokeSpecialTest`]( but this one correctly throws `IllegalAccessError`, so the type test is bypassed only sometimes.

I get the correct result from OpenJ9 if it is built as Java 8, or if it is built as Java 11 and JIT options force the `nosey` method to be compiled. But if `nosey` is interpreted in Java 11, I don't get an exception.
The problem appears to have been introduced by #2434. If I build with that commit reverted, I get the exception again.
I tried to reduce the test case further with [`InterfaceInvokeSpecialTest`]( but this one correctly throws `IllegalAccessError`, so the type test is bypassed only sometimes.

issue_title: invokespecial updates
description:
See #1730
invokespecial checks for NULL receiver before resolution. It needs a resolution check in the NPE case similar the invokevirtual/invokeinterface.

issue_title: Java 11 nest member and host must be loaded by same classloader?
description:
`OpenJ9 vm/visible.c:loadAndVerifyNestHost()` assumes that nest host and members must be loaded by same classloader as following comments:
/* Nest host must be successfully loaded by the same classloader in the same package & verify the nest member */
Is it possible there are two custom class loaders (one is another's ancestor) such that one loads nest host and anther loads nest members?
Specification states:
public Class<?> getNestHost()
`SecurityException` - If the returned class is not the current class, and if a security manager, `s`, is present and the caller's class loader is not the same as or an ancestor of the class loader for the returned class and invocation of `s.checkPackageAccess()` denies access to the package of the returned class.
Apparently current `java.lang.Class.getNestHost()/getNestMembers()` haven't performed security check yet.
FYI: @tajila @DanHeidinga

issue_title: Convert PullRequest builds to be "pipeline of jobs"
description:
Related #1450 Currently our PR builds execute in a single job. We use our OpenJ9 build AND test pipeline scripts in order to complete the build. This is inefficient because it is a different process than how all our other builds are now working. In order to complete #1450 and remove our test pipeline code, we need to convert the PR builds to use the [Pipeline-Build-Test-Any-Platform]( This will also allow for other PR work to proceed. There are two parts in order to get this working
1. Reconfig the PR jobs to use the above file instead of the matching PR files
1a. Add the PLATFORM, SDK_VERSION and TESTS_TARGETS (not TEST_TARGET or TEST_TARGETS) parameters to each PR job
1. Modify the pipeline files ([1]( to pass the PR related parameters we need in the build.
 - ghprbPullId
 - ghprbGhRepository
 - ghprbCommentBody
 - ghprbTargetBranch
/cc @llxia @jdekonin @vsebe

issue_title: Convert OMR Acceptance build to use Pipeline-Build-Test-All
description:
Related #2728 #1897 #2272 #2160 The [OMR-Acceptance build]( currently uses its own top level [pipeline file]( that calls Build and Test jobs directly ([workflow function]( This is inconsistent with how the other builds work and has proven to be a pain point as we make changes to the pipelines (eg. #2272). [Pipeline-Build-Test-All]( was introduced as a reusable top level "build what you want" file. We should reuse this file rather than maintaining two separate files that do somewhat the same thing.
The most notable differences will be:
- OMR build will now be 3 levels deep like the nightly build (currently only 2 levels)
 - i.e OMR -> Pipeline-B-T-JDKX-SPEC -> Build-JDKX-SPEC
- Slack notifications will no longer indicate the build is OMR
- Current:
Failure in: Pipeline-OMR-Acceptance #731 (Open)
Downstream Job: Test-sanity.functional-JDK8-win_x86-64_cmprssptrs #73 (Open)
 - New: Failure in: Pipeline-Build-Test-JDK8-win_x86-64_cmprssptrs #20 (Open)
Downstream Job: Test-sanity.functional-JDK8-win_x86-64_cmprssptrs #73 (Open)
Note: We could add something to the output to indicate upstream job name.
Other considerations:
- The current build has a hack in order to run the cmake spec (compile only). This would have to be investigated on how to add it to the new style build. (cc @dnakamura )
- This would also add win32 (jdk8 only) to the build which is not currently added. The logic in order to only run it on 8 exists in Pipe-B-T-All but hasn't been copied into the current OMR pipe file. Converting the build would eliminate the need to copy this logic.
Changes Required:
- The OMR build would need to point to the P-B-T-All pipeline file instead of the current one
- The OMR Pipe can be deleted
- Add Params to the OMR Build
 - OMR_BRANCH = master
 - Java8 = true
 - Java10 = true
 - TESTS_TARGETS = sanity.functional
- Some logic would need to be added to the end of P-B-T-All in order to fire the Promotion at the end of the build.
cc @jdekonin @vsebe

issue_title: Add "Any Target" test job(s) to PR builds
description:
Helps #2316
Depends #2728 Sometimes it would be useful to only run a smaller set of testing for PR builds. We should be able to add a set of jobs that would accept any test target. Very similar to the [Grinder job]( We likely need them per spec and per platform because our pipelines call the existing test jobs without passing that information. We also currently do not pass the BUILD_LIST for PR jobs so we would have to hardcode the default parameter to be `functional,system'. This would cause a bit more overhead for the setup time, but would allow us to call any target from either test set.
creator: AdamBrousseau

issue_title: Verify signal handler registration for SIG_RI_INTERRUPT
description:
Signal handler for `SIG_RI_INTERRUPT` is registered in `linuxs390/j9ri.c`.
1) [j9ri_enableRISupport](
2) [j9ri_disableRISupport](
OMRSIG_SIGACTION(SIG_RI_INTERRUPT, NULL, NULL)
The above code is used in `j9ri_enableRISupport` and `j9ri_disableRISupport`. The above code translates to a `nop` in case of `sigaction`. In case of `omrsig_primary_sigaction`, the above code will return `-1`.
I think the goal is to unregister handler for `SIG_RI_INTERRUPT` while restoring the original handler. If so, the old handler`needs to be cached and passed as an input.
 Correct usage During registration:
OMRSIG_SIGACTION(SIG_RI_INTERRUPT, &newAction, &oldAction)
During unregistration:
OMRSIG_SIGACTION(SIG_RI_INTERRUPT, &oldAction, NULL)

issue_title: issue about notification for exceeding CollectionUsageThresold of tenure MemoryPool
description:
Base on documentation of MemoryNotificationInfo.MEMORY_COLLECTION_THRESHOLD_EXCEEDED
> Notification type denoting that the memory usage of a memory pool is greater than or equal to its collection usage threshold after the Java virtual machine has expended effort in recycling unused objects in that memory pool. This notification is emitted by MemoryMXBean.
So we should only check the tenure memory pool if MEMORY_COLLECTION_THRESHOLD_EXCEEDED after global GC because scavenge GC does not recycle tenure memory pool.
 Currently we check and fire notification for tenure pool after every GC(both global and scavenge).

issue_title: JVMTI extensions event com.openj9.PatchToJavaBase
description:
I'm implementing a JVMTI extensions event with behavior similar to `--patch-module` but available at `Agent_OnLoad` so classes can be defined into java.base early in startup. When the event is triggered it will run a callback function with the class name giving the user the option to respond whether or not this class should be loaded into java.base or the unnamed module. Something along the lines of:
`jboolean JNICALL PatchToJavaBase(jvmtiEnv *jvmti_env, JNIEnv* jni_env, char* className)`
this event was first discussed as a solution to #2751. the benefits of this event are in making the class's module an explicit choice rather than an implementation detail.
fyi @DanHeidinga

description:
>A class or interface C is accessible to a class or interface D if and only if one of the following is true:

issue_title: Potential deadlock for calling GarbageCollectorMXBean.getLastGcInfo()
description:
native method getLastGcInfoImp() hold managementDataLock(for read) for retrieving GC Information,
during constructing memory pool name(Java String), it could trigger GC due to allocation failure.
GCStartEvent would require managementDataLock (for write) to update memory usage Data in vm structures. it would cause a deadlock.

issue_title: Investigate limiting System.identityHashcode() to positive numbers
description:
OpenJ9 allows both positive and negative identity hashcodes. This is problematic for programs that incorrectly assume hashcodes can only be positive.
Investigate adding an option to limit hashcode to be positive and determine the performance overhead of this.
Note, any such option would limit the range of hashcodes and may lead to more collisions.

Will start recording initial findings in this issue. Some tests hang, so the set of tests have to be run is small groups, not sanity.functional or extended.functional as those large targets both contain tests that hang.
**Testing with: java -version**
openjdk version "9.0.4-internal"
OpenJDK Runtime Environment (build 9.0.4-internal+0-adhoc.nazim.nasm-osx-pr-build)
Eclipse OpenJ9 VM (build nasm-initial-wip-b067ee64, JRE 9 Darwin amd64-64-Bit 20181001_000000 (JIT enabled, AOT enabled)
OpenJ9 - b067ee64
OMR - fe8efc6c
JCL - 361429b612 based on jdk-9.0.4+12)
**Test targets that fail:**
AttachAPISanity_0 - [attachapisanity_report.html.txt]( #3206
jsr292Test_0, jsr292Test_1 - [jsr292Test_1_report.html.txt]( @fengxue-IS Is looking at these
JLM_Tests_interface - [JLM_Tests-report.html.txt]( @JasonFengJ9 is looking at these
SoftmxRASTest1, SoftmxRASTest2 - [SoftmxRASTest_report.html.txt](
J9vmTest - all fail, [TestTargetResult_J9vmTest.tap.txt]( @pdbain-ibm looked at these
 (as expected with Darwin is not a supported OS platform error)
in cmdLineTests dir: (Sanity: TOTAL: 81 EXECUTED: 81 PASSED: 2 FAILED: 79 SKIPPED: 0)
(Extended: TOTAL: 83 EXECUTED: 83 PASSED: 0 FAILED: 83 SKIPPED: 0)
Most cmdLineTests fail with " Darwin is not a supported OS platform"
Some variants of cmdLineTester_GCRegressionTests - fail with JVMJ9VM007E Command-line option unrecognised: -Xgcpolicy:metronome - @pdbain-ibm can you look at this?
Error: Could not create the Java Virtual Machine.
Error: A fatal exception has occurred. Program will exit.
**Test targets that hang:**
jsr292Test_JitCount0_0
IllegalAccessProtectedMethodTest_0
jit_jitt_0 (hangs at cfgTest subtest)
VarHandleInvokerTest_1 To reproduce ([install test prereqs]( on machine if not present):
1. Unpack jdk9 openj9 osx SDK to /someLocation
2. git clone (to /testLocation)
3. cd openjdk-tests
4. ./get.sh -t /testLocation/openjdk-tests -p x64_mac -i openj9
5. cd TestConfig
6. export environment variables ( export JAVA_BIN=/someLocation/bin export SPEC=macos_x86-64 export JDK_VERSION=9 export JDK_IMPL=openj9 export BUILD_LIST=functional ) Reminder: JDK_VERSION=11, if you are testing a JDK11 build.
7. make -f run_configure.mk
8. make compile (DDR_Test requires ddrtools to compile, if your build does not have that, quick workaround is to delete openjdk-tests/functional/DDR_Test directory, all other test dirs compile)
9. make _AttachAPISanity_0 (or any other of the failing targets listed above, prepended with _)
Note: to run all sanity tests inside a directory of tests, for step 9, can use:
make -C ../functional/UnsafeTest -f autoGen.mk _sanity
or _extended to run all extended tests in the dir

issue_title: OpenJ9 OSX JDK doesn't work on older MacOS versions
description:
OpenJ9 OSX JDK11 was built on MacOS version `10.13.4`. The JDK worked fine on the machine where it was built:
$ java -version
openjdk version "11-internal" 2018-09-25
OpenJDK Runtime Environment (build 11-internal+0-adhoc.sbabneetcaibmcom.openj9-openjdk-jdk11)
Eclipse OpenJ9 VM (build master-efb8194d2, JRE 11 Darwin amd64-64-Bit Compressed References 20181011_000000 (JIT enabled, AOT enabled)
OpenJ9 - efb8194d2
OMR - e8f52374
JCL - 8356813ad5 based on jdk-11+28)
On an older MacOS version `10.12.6`, the above JDK didn't work. The following error was seen:
$ java -version
libjvm.so preloadLibrary(/Users/pdbain/vm/jdk/lib/default/libj9vm29.dylib): dlopen(/Users/pdbain/vm/jdk/lib/default/libj9vm29.dylib, 2): Symbol not found: _syslog$DARWIN_EXTSN
 Referenced from: /Users/pdbain/vm/jdk/lib/default/libj9prt29.dylib (which was built for Mac OS X 10.13)
 Expected in: /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib
 in /Users/pdbain/vm/jdk/lib/default/libj9prt29.dylib
libjvm.so failed to load: j9vm29
`openj9-openjdk-jdk*` extension repos specify the following option: `-mmacosx-version-min=10.9.0`.
Based upon the above error, `-mmacosx-version-min=10.9.0` doesn't get applied when building the port library (`libj9prt29.dylib`). The above error may go away if the port library is build using `-mmacosx-version-min=10.9.0`. Will have to verify if this change resolves the issue.

issue_title: Setup OSX Machines for JDK8
description:
## Setting up the machine
- Install Mac OS X 10.10 (Yosemite)
- The instructions below must be executed with `sudo` permissions.
- Install brew
/usr/bin/ruby -e "$(curl -fsSL - Download Xcode 4.6.3 from sudo mkdir /Applications/Xcode4
- Drag Xcode.app for Xcode4 into /Applications/Xcode4. Alternate command line variant to mount and copy the Xcode dmg file. This will help in automating the setup process on OSX machines:
# Mount the Xcode dmg file
hdiutil attach /path/to/XCODE.dmg
# Copy Xcode.app to the desired location
cp -a /Volumes/Xcode/Xcode.app <PATH_TO_DESIRED_LOCATION>
# Unmout the Xcode dmg file
hdiutil detach /dev/disk...
- Download Xcode 7.2.1 from sudo mkdir /Applications/Xcode7
- Drag Xcode.app for Xcode7 into /Applications/Xcode7. The above command line variant can be used to mount and copy Xcode7 to a desired location. brew won't allow gcc-4.9 to be installed with Xcode4. So, switch to Xcode7.
sudo xcode-select -switch /Applications/Xcode7/Xcode.app
- Accept Xcode license if needed.
sudo xcodebuild -license accept
- Install Bash version 4. Instructions: `./get_source.sh` asks for Bash version 4. Bash version 4 will be located here: `/usr/local/bin/bash`. Extension repo scripts will try to use `/bin/bash`. `/bin/bash` will point to Bash version 3 after installing Bash version 4. Associate `/bin/bash` symlink to Bash version 4:
rm -f /bin/bash
ln -s /usr/local/bin/bash /bin/bash
- Install gnu-sed. Default `sed` on OSX won't process carriage returns (`\r`) and new-lines (`\n`). `gsed` will doesn't have this issue.
brew install gnu-sed
- Install gnu-tar. Default `tar` on OSX doesn't support `--exclude-vcs` option where `gtar` supports `--exclude-vcs`.
brew install gnu-tar
- Install other required tools.
brew install nasm autoconf git freetype
- Only required on OSX 10.10 (Yosemite). Edit **line 143** (`typedef void (^dispatch_block_t)(void);`) in **/usr/include/dispatch/object.h**:
#ifdef __clang__
typedef void (^dispatch_block_t)(void);
#else
typedef void* dispatch_block_t;
#endif
## Building OpenJ9 JDK8
- Download the boot JDK from AdoptOpenJDK. Technically, JDK7 should be used as the boot JDK but JDK7 isn't available at AdoptOpenJDK. So, I used OpenJDK8 with Hotspot as the boot JDK, and no issues were seen: - Clone openj9-openjdk-jdk8 extensions repo:
git clone cd ./openj9-openjdk-jdk8
- Download and unzip `freemarker.jar`:
wget -O freemarker.tgz
gtar -xzf freemarker.tgz freemarker-2.3.8/lib/freemarker.jar --strip-components=2
rm -f freemarker.tgz
The default BSD `tar` on Mac won't strip component. `gtar` should be used to `--strip-components`.
- Set the following environment variables:
export SED=gsed
export TAR=gtar
export MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=10.9.0
export SDKPATH=/Applications/Xcode4/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/MacOSX.platform/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX10.8.sdk
export JAVA_HOME=<PATH_TO_BOOT_JDK>
^^^ Make sure that the above file and executable paths are valid on the machine. ^^^
- Info about the above environment variables:
# SED=gsed overrides the default sed OSX since it doesn't process new lines \n and carriage returns \r.
# TAR=gtar overrides the default tar on OSX since it doesn't support --exclude-vcs option.
# Setting UMA_SUPPRESS_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS and OMR_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS: warnings won't be treated as errors.
# If MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET is not set to 10.9.0, ./configure will fail.
# SDKPATH points to the Xcode4 SDK directory
# JAVA_HOME should point to the boot JDK.
- Run `./configure`:
# Compressedrefs
bash ./configure \
 --with-freemarker-jar=<PATH_TO_FREEMARKER_JAR> \
 --with-xcode-path=<PATH_TO_XCODE4_APP> \
 --with-openj9-cc=<PATH_TO_OPENJ9_CC> \
 --with-openj9-cxx=<PATH_TO_OPENJ9_CXX> \
 --with-openj9-developer-dir=<PATH_TO_OPENJ9_DEVELOPER_DIR>
# Non-compressedrefs
bash ./configure \
 --with-freemarker-jar=<PATH_TO_FREEMARKER_JAR> \
 --with-xcode-path=<PATH_TO_XCODE4_APP> \
 --with-openj9-cc=<PATH_TO_OPENJ9_CC> \
 --with-openj9-cxx=<PATH_TO_OPENJ9_CXX> \
 --with-openj9-developer-dir=<PATH_TO_OPENJ9_DEVELOPER_DIR> \
 --with-noncompressedrefs
PATH_TO_XCODE4_APP=/Applications/Xcode4/Xcode.app
PATH_TO_OPENJ9_CC=<POINT_TO_XCODE7_CLANG>
PATH_TO_OPENJ9_CXX=<POINT_TO_XCODE7_CLANG++>
PATH_TO_OPENJ9_DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode7/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer
# OPENJ9_DEVELOPER_DIR, OPENJ9_CC and OPENJ9_CXX are used to specify custom
# tools to build OpenJ9. The default tools Xcode4 + gcc-4.2 will fail to build OpenJ9.
- Run `make`:
# Variant 1
make all
# In JDK8, build.log isn't generated. Also, make's output may have insufficient info for debugging.
# For debugging, make can be run as follows:
make LOG=trace all 2>&1 | tee make_images.log
# Shorter and quicker variant if one doesn't want to run "make all".
make images
If `make` is successful, a `j2sdk-images` and a `j2re-image` should be generated in the `build` directory.

issue_title: Agent support for exception catch information
description:
This Epic tracks the work to enable agents to request exception catch information without the JVM going into Full Speed Debug (FSD) mode. Most of the work here is on the VM side but there are JIT portions as well to ensure we have a stack map at the start of every exception catch block and to ensure we don't enable throw to goto transformations when this mode is enabled.
Other than the obvious desire to enable as many features as possible without going into FSD, the motivation behind this work is the upcoming cooperation with OverOps - their agent needs to get exception events, but can not tolerate the overhead of FSD being imposed on production systems.

issue_title: Always fill in return values in JVMTI
description:
GetOwnedMonitorStackDepthInfo (and quite likely others) does not always fill in the return buffer pointer (in particular, if there are no monitors, the call returns success, fills in the buffer size to 0, but does not fill in the buffer pointer with NULL.
All JVMTI calls return an error code. Any other returned information is done via pointers passed to the function. The specification states that the return values will be filled in - it does not say that the call has to return success in order to do so.

issue_title: JEP 331 design and implementation notes
description:
## Overview of JEP 331 : Low-Overhead Heap Profiling
Provide a low-overhead way to sample Java heap allocations via `JVMTI` interface.
Specifically, this feature is low-overhead enough to be enabled by default, allocation sampling interval can be set via a new `JVMTI API`, and a callback can provide heap object info being allocated. When the event is generated and the callback is invoked, a stack trace can be captured with an existing `JVMTI GetStackTrace` method, in addition, the `jobect` reference from the callback can be wrapped into a `JNI weak reference` which can be used later to determine if the object is still alive.
Note: this feature is optional for VM implementations, a new capability is introduced to indicate if VM has implemented this JEP.
## Details
`VM/GC/OMR` changes are required to support this JEP feature.
 VM changes proposed:
Add following new define and API from [JVMTI v11](
- `JVMTI v11` version define:
          `#define JVMTI_VERSION_11_0 <hex>` - A new capability:
          `unsigned int can_generate_sampled_object_alloc_events : 1;`
- A new event:
          `JVMTI_EVENT_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOC = 86,`
- A new callback:
 void JNICALL SampledObjectAlloc(
 jvmtiEnv *jvmti_env,
 JNIEnv* jni_env,
 jthread thread,
 jobject object,
 jclass object_klass,
 jlong size)
 - A new JVMTI method:
          `jvmtiError SetHeapSamplingInterval(jvmtiEnv* env, jint sampling_interval)`
- A new callback:
          `jvmtiError SetHeapSamplingInterval(jvmtiEnv* env, jint sampling_interval)`
Add a new hook event:      `J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE` which can be trigged via `TRIGGER_J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE`.
 GC changes proposed:
Add a method to set sampling interval:
          `void j9gc_set_allocation_sampling_interval(J9VMThread *vmThread, UDATA samplingInterval)`
 Disable inline TLH allocation:
           Force `JIT/Interpreter` to perform out of line allocation if the event `J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE` is registered, i.e., call `J9AllocateObject` or `J9AllocateIndexableObject`. This is similar with existing `J9HOOK_VM_OBJECT_ALLOCATE_INSTRUMENTABLE` or `J9HOOK_VM_OBJECT_ALLOCATE_WITHIN_THRESHOLD`.
           `MM_GCExtensions::getExtensions(env)->instrumentableAllocateHookEnabled` can be reused as the flag to disable inline TLH allocation. Also noticed that `instrumentableAllocateHookEnabled` is only referred within `mgcalloc.cpp:memoryManagerTLHAsyncCallbackHandler()`, maybe it can be replaced with a local variable?
Invoke the callback:
           Within `J9AllocateObject()` or `J9AllocateIndexableObject()`, following trigger method for the event callback is going to be called according to `extensions->allocationSamplingInterval` and `extensions->currentAllocationRemainder` (to be added within `OMR GCExtensionsBase.hpp`).
 TRIGGER_J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE(
 vmThread->javaVM->hookInterface, vmThread,
 objectPtr, sizeInBytesRequired);
Note that the sampling interval is not precise hence not introducing lock to ensure exclusive update of `currentAllocationRemainder`.
 OMR changes proposed:
Add two variables within `GCExtensionsBase.hpp` which can be get/set via `MM_GCExtensions`:
 uintptr_t allocationSamplingInterval; /**< the heap sampling interval */
 uintptr_t currentAllocationRemainder; /**< the remainder of current allocation size modulo the heap sampling interval */
 ## Performance target:
If the event `J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE` is not registered, there is no noticeable performance overhead;
If the event `J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE` is registered but the callback `SampledAllocEvent` is empty and no callback is performed with default 512K interval, the overhead is `~1%`;
If the event `J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE` is registered and the callback `SampledAllocEvent` captures a `StackTrace` and/or create a a `JNI weak reference` to the `jobject` returned by the callback, the overhead is `~3%`.
Note: these targets aim to match `RI` that was described in [JEP 331]( The benchmark in question might be `Dacapo` or `DayTrader` about `throughput` or `startup`.
## Test Plan
Add `OpenJ9` tests:
- Verify that `capability can_generate_sampled_object_alloc_events` presents;
- Verify that `JVMTI_EVENT_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOC`can be turned on or off, i.e., the callback is invoked or not accordingly;
- Verify that callback returns correct objects being allocated;
- Verify that sampling interval is respected;
- Verify that `StackTrace` captured is as expected;
- Verify that a `JNI weak reference` to the `jobject` reference returned by the callback can be used to determine if the object is alive;
## Potential enhancements
Trigger the event `J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE` according to `ClassLoader` (`BOOT_LOADER`, `PLATFORM_LOADER`, `APP_LOADER` or customer classloaders), `thread`, `object_klass` and/or `size`. Could work with existing `lowAllocationThreshold`, `highAllocationThreshold`, `oolObjectSamplingBytesGranularity`, `frequentObjectAllocationSamplingRate`, etc. ## Documentation
Document update, blog creation, etc.
## Others
This feature doesn't affect existing application. There is no migration effort required for this specific feature. No security issue is expected.
Overall the risk is medium.

When the event is generated and the callback is invoked, a stack trace can be captured with an existing `JVMTI GetStackTrace` method, in addition, the `jobect` reference from the callback can be wrapped into a `JNI weak reference` which can be used later to determine if the object is still alive.
Note: this feature is optional for VM implementations, a new capability is introduced to indicate if VM has implemented this JEP.
## Details
`VM/GC/OMR` changes are required to support this JEP feature.
 VM changes proposed:
Add following new define and API from [JVMTI v11](
- `JVMTI v11` version define:
          `#define JVMTI_VERSION_11_0 <hex>` - A new capability:
          `unsigned int can_generate_sampled_object_alloc_events : 1;`
- A new event:
          `JVMTI_EVENT_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOC = 86,`
- A new callback:
 void JNICALL SampledObjectAlloc(
 jvmtiEnv *jvmti_env,
 JNIEnv* jni_env,
 jthread thread,
 jobject object,
 jclass object_klass,
 jlong size)
 - A new JVMTI method:
          `jvmtiError SetHeapSamplingInterval(jvmtiEnv* env, jint sampling_interval)`
- A new callback:
          `jvmtiError SetHeapSamplingInterval(jvmtiEnv* env, jint sampling_interval)`
Add a new hook event:      `J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE` which can be trigged via `TRIGGER_J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE`.
 GC changes proposed:
Add a method to set sampling interval:
          `void j9gc_set_allocation_sampling_interval(J9VMThread *vmThread, UDATA samplingInterval)`
 Disable inline TLH allocation:
           Force `JIT/Interpreter` to perform out of line allocation if the event `J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE` is registered, i.e., call `J9AllocateObject` or `J9AllocateIndexableObject`. This is similar with existing `J9HOOK_VM_OBJECT_ALLOCATE_INSTRUMENTABLE` or `J9HOOK_VM_OBJECT_ALLOCATE_WITHIN_THRESHOLD`.
           `MM_GCExtensions::getExtensions(env)->instrumentableAllocateHookEnabled` can be reused as the flag to disable inline TLH allocation. Also noticed that `instrumentableAllocateHookEnabled` is only referred within `mgcalloc.cpp:memoryManagerTLHAsyncCallbackHandler()`, maybe it can be replaced with a local variable?
Invoke the callback:
           Within `J9AllocateObject()` or `J9AllocateIndexableObject()`, following trigger method for the event callback is going to be called according to `extensions->allocationSamplingInterval` and `extensions->currentAllocationRemainder` (to be added within `OMR GCExtensionsBase.hpp`).
 TRIGGER_J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE(
 vmThread->javaVM->hookInterface, vmThread,
 objectPtr, sizeInBytesRequired);
Note that the sampling interval is not precise hence not introducing lock to ensure exclusive update of `currentAllocationRemainder`.
 OMR changes proposed:
Add two variables within `GCExtensionsBase.hpp` which can be get/set via `MM_GCExtensions`:
 uintptr_t allocationSamplingInterval; /**< the heap sampling interval */
 uintptr_t currentAllocationRemainder; /**< the remainder of current allocation size modulo the heap sampling interval */
 ## Performance target:
If the event `J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE` is not registered, there is no noticeable performance overhead;
If the event `J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE` is registered but the callback `SampledAllocEvent` is empty and no callback is performed with default 512K interval, the overhead is `~1%`;
If the event `J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE` is registered and the callback `SampledAllocEvent` captures a `StackTrace` and/or create a a `JNI weak reference` to the `jobject` returned by the callback, the overhead is `~3%`.
Note: these targets aim to match `RI` that was described in [JEP 331]( The benchmark in question might be `Dacapo` or `DayTrader` about `throughput` or `startup`.
## Test Plan
Add `OpenJ9` tests:
- Verify that `capability can_generate_sampled_object_alloc_events` presents;
- Verify that `JVMTI_EVENT_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOC`can be turned on or off, i.e., the callback is invoked or not accordingly;
- Verify that callback returns correct objects being allocated;
- Verify that sampling interval is respected;
- Verify that `StackTrace` captured is as expected;
- Verify that a `JNI weak reference` to the `jobject` reference returned by the callback can be used to determine if the object is alive;
## Potential enhancements
Trigger the event `J9HOOK_SAMPLED_OBJECT_ALLOCATE` according to `ClassLoader` (`BOOT_LOADER`, `PLATFORM_LOADER`, `APP_LOADER` or customer classloaders), `thread`, `object_klass` and/or `size`. Could work with existing `lowAllocationThreshold`, `highAllocationThreshold`, `oolObjectSamplingBytesGranularity`, `frequentObjectAllocationSamplingRate`, etc. ## Documentation
Document update, blog creation, etc.
## Others
This feature doesn't affect existing application. There is no migration effort required for this specific feature. No security issue is expected.
Overall the risk is medium.

issue_title: ghftm001 test failed with Concurrent Scavenge
description:
JVMTI Test ghftm001.java initiates GC cycle and waiting (sleeping) for GC Cycle End event.
However current implementation of Concurrent Scavenger does not force final STW Scavenge to complete cycle but expect it to be triggered by next Allocation Failure. So, because there is no further allocation in the test it reached timeout and failed eventually.
Concurrent Scavenger should force final STW Scavenge as soon as concurrent phase is complete.

issue_title: Investigate Compressing Jenkins build logs
description:
Jenkins Compress build log plugin
Issue:
Pipeline Compatibility
From version 1.1, the Compress Build Log Plugin supports compressing full pipeline build logs, but not the per-step build logs stored separately.
What this means, The overall log is essentially duplicated/separated into each step as a separate numbered log file. The overall log which has all the output will be replaced with a `gz` compressed version but each step will not be compressed. I have tried removing the individual step logs. This removes the steps from the blue ocean view. I have also tried gzipping the numbered logs but this is the same result as deleting them.
See
Compress pipeline stage logs?
Optimize log handling in Pipeline and Durable Task
External Build Log storage for Jenkins

issue_title: Enable minimum ALS asserts as fatal and add `-Xjit:disable<arch>` testing
description:
Since the introduction of the `minimumALS` property for each instruction we've introduced a nice assert in OMR which asserts [1] that the instruction we're about to generated is supported on the architecture we're running on. This prevents the common bugs of forgetting to guard a particular piece of evaluator with an architecture guard. These will result as SIGILL failures in production.
Unfortunately one shortcoming of the current implementation is that the assert is non-fatal, meaning it will not fire at the moment unless we're in a debug compilation, which is pretty much never. Another shortcoming is that there are instructions which have a `TR_UnknownArchitecture` ALS. These are typically pseudo-instructions. They will actually trigger those asserts always. We need to fix that as well.
What I propose here is the following:
1. Enable the asserts to be fatal
2. Take a look at which instructions have a `TR_UnknownArchitecture` ALS and see if we can modify them to use `TR_LatestArchitecture` instead. If we can eliminate `TR_UnknownArchitecture` from OMRInstOpCodeProperties then everything will work.
3. Add OpenJ9 tests on some simple workload, possibly even `java -version` with variants of every single `-Xjit:disable<arch>` that we support so we catch all these bugs right at the PR level before they're checked in
[1]

issue_title: Remove specialized wide bytecodes
description: Given how infrequently wide bytecodes are used, there seems little point optimizing them in the interpreter. I suggest removing iloadw, etc and going back to "wide iload". This reclaims some space in the bytecode table at what will almost certainly be no performance cost (JITted code will be completely unaffected by this change).

issue_title: Investigate use of transparent large pages when set to [madvise]
description:

always [madvise] never
Investigate whether we should use `MADV_HUGEPAGE` & `madvise` to allocate the heap and / or the code cache.

description:
The following tests are failing in ... [Sanity - JDK11 - osx_x86-64_cmprssptrs]( SUMMARY OF FAILED TESTS
 abort softwareFloat hardwareFloat softwareRead hardwareRead abort thread
 softwareFloat thread
 hardwareFloat thread
 softwareRead thread
 hardwareRead thread
The reason for the above test failures is `UnsatisfiedLinkError`:
 [ERR] Exception in thread "main" java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: gptest (Not found in java.library.path)
 [ERR] at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.loadLibraryWithPath(ClassLoader.java:1678)
 [ERR] at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.loadLibraryWithClassLoader(ClassLoader.java:1648)
 [ERR] at java.base/java.lang.System.loadLibrary(System.java:559)
 [ERR] at VMBench.GPTests.GPTest.<clinit>(GPTest.java:70)
To fix the above test failures, test infrastructure needs to set `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` on MacOSX instead of `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
