issue_title: New ValueType access flag ACC_PERMITS_VALUE
description:
With the introduction of value class and primitive class to project Valhalla in the latest spec, the access flag `ACC_ATOMIC (<hex>)` is removed. This bit is now `ACC_PERMITS_VALUE`. For value types that requires atomic access, value class should be used. This means the change to previous [issue]( can be reverted and OpenJ9 needs to recognize and support `ACC_PERMITS_VALUE`.
From > An abstract class that allows value subclasses declares this capability in its class file using the ACC_PERMITS_VALUE modifier (<hex>). At class load time, an error occurs if the class is not abstract, declares an instance field, declares a synchronized method, or implements—directly or indirectly—IdentityObject.
Also from the latest [spec](
> If the ACC_FINAL flag is set, ......ACC_PERMITS_VALUE flags must not be set.
> If the ACC_VALUE flag is set, the ACC_FINAL flag must also be set, and the ACC_ABSTRACT, ACC_PERMITS_VALUE, ACC_ENUM, ACC_INTERFACE, and ACC_MODULE flags must not be set.
> if C is a value class or an abstract class with its ACC_PERMITS_VALUE flag set, and the class or interface named as the direct superclass of C does not have its ACC_PERMITS_VALUE flag set, loading throws an IncompatibleClassChangeError.

issue_title: Variable length arguments of jvmtiExtensionFunction
creator: knn-k
text:
Bug Title: Variable length arguments of jvmtiExtensionFunction
Bug Description: I found the following issue with the definition of `jvmtiExtensionFunction`. There is a mismatch in the placement of the arguments for variadic functions between the caller side and the callee side. It causes a serious problem on AArch64 macOS, but all other platforms are also affected.
`jvmtiExtensionFunction` is defined as follows in jvmti.h. It is a function pointer with variable length arguments.
typedef jvmtiError (JNICALL *jvmtiExtensionFunction)
 (jvmtiEnv *jvmti_env, ...);
 contains the bodies of JVMTI extension functions. Look at the prototypes of some of them:
static jvmtiError JNICALL jvmtiGetHeapFreeMemory(jvmtiEnv* jvmti_env, jlong* heapFree_ptr, ...);
static jvmtiError JNICALL jvmtiGetHeapTotalMemory(jvmtiEnv* jvmti_env, jlong* heapTotal_ptr, ...);
static jvmtiError JNICALL jvmtiIterateSharedCaches(jvmtiEnv* env, jint version, const char *cacheDir, jint flags, jboolean useCommandLineValues, jvmtiIterateSharedCachesCallback callback, void *user_data, ...);
They take different numbers of arguments of different types.
Let's take a look at `jvmtiIterateSharedCaches()` for example.
Its assembly code expects `env` to be in the register `x0`, `version` in `x1`, `cacheDir` in `x2`, and so on, on AArch64 macOS.
On the other side, its test code in the system test places the arguments `version` and after that on the stack because they are `...` in the `jvmtiExtensionFunction` prototype.
It does not work as expected, of course.

issue_title: Serviceability Request: Add context class loader to Thread details in javacore.txt
description:
This issue is a serviceability request, that a thread's context class loader (the `Thread.contextClassLoader` field) be included in the summary of thread information in the Thread Details section of a javacore. In some support scenarios, it's useful to know the context class loader of a thread at the time an issue occurs, but under current circumstances that information is only available by either modifying the Java application to explicitly print that value or by inspecting a full system core. As javacores are much leaner and more accessible than system cores (not to mention much more reliably created and collected), particularly for issues around thread behavior, this would be a quicker way to get at that information without having to rely on the application - in support scenarios, an application may not be modifiable by the person working with the support agent.
The information wouldn't need to be terribly detailed - the class loader type and address, as in the `CLTEXTCLLOADER` entries later in the javacore, would be perfectly sufficient (any additional details can come from finding that object in the `CLASSES` section of the javacore). There is already some detail on threads' attributes in the Thread Details section (daemon status, native ID, etc.), so my thought is that this could be included along with that information.
Feel free to let me know if you have any additional thoughts or questions for me regarding this request.

issue_title: CRIU: Address isCheckpointAllowed bootstrapping issues
description:
Current, if one calls `isCheckpointAllowed` before `isCRIUSupportEnabled` this may result in a linkage error.
To fix this we should rename the native to add `impl` and create a new wrapper `isCheckpointAllowed` that calls `isCRIUSupportEnabled` before calling the native.
Also, in `checkpointJVM` we should use `isCheckpointAllowed` instead of `isCRIUSupportEnabled`

issue_title: Reducing memory footprint by disclaiming AOT memory after load
description: During a warm run, once the JIT detects that it has exited start-up it will disclaim the AOT region of the shared class cache to reduce memory footprint, since the methods of that region will already have been loaded into the code cache of the JVM. It is possible to reduce the footprint after load, possibly by issuing another disclaim a few minutes after load.
creator: cjjdespres
text:

Bug Description: During a warm run, once the JIT detects that it has exited start-up it will disclaim the AOT region of the shared class cache to reduce memory footprint, since the methods of that region will already have been loaded into the code cache of the JVM. It is possible to reduce the footprint after load, possibly by issuing another disclaim a few minutes after load.

issue_title: Class.getDeclaredConstructors should search for unnamed factory methods on value classes
description:
A new kind of special method, unnamed factory methods are introduced to create the instances of a value class. Unnamed factory methods are named `<new>` and are static. They return an instance of the value class. From the [Value Objects JEP](
`The method Class.getDeclaredConstructors, and related methods, search for unnamed factory methods rather than instance initialization methods when invoked on a value class.`

issue_title: ValueTypes: Add support for reference projection arrays
description:
In the current model, a given primitive type can have two types, the primary type and the reference projection (AKA the box).
Using `Point` as an example:
public primitive class Point {
...
}
Point p = new Point(..); //primary
Point.ref pRef = null; //reference projection
pRef = p;
As a result there are two types of arrays, `Point[]` (the primary type array) and `Point.ref[]` (the reference projection) they are allocated with classrefs `"QPoint;"` and `Point` respectively. Note that the first one is a signature and the second is a simple name.
It is possible to instantiate `new Point.ref[size]` but not `new Point.ref(...)`
Point[] p = new Point[size]; //primary
Point.ref[] pRef = new Point.ref[size]; //reference projection
This will require updates to our classfile parsers and potentially romclass builders
See for java class file encoding
In the JVM we will need two J9Class'es, one for the primitive type, and the other for the value reference projection. I'm not sure that we will need two ROM classes, but thats something we will need to think about.

issue_title: The loop in DsaStackFrame.findSfxm() needs to be improved.
description:
There is a case in which user is looking for help to understand an OutofMemoryError, followed by a GPF crash. They have collected dumps, but there are some issues with opening the dumps in tools like Memory Analyzer, jdpmview and other tools that use the DTFJ API.
All the dumps requested by IEATDUMP - after the OOM occurs - ended with a return code 2, reason code 4, which means:
Return code Reason code 00000004 00000002 Meaning: Contention detected when attempting to set tasks in the address space non-dispatchable.
Action: Data in dump may be inconsistent. Reissue IEATDUMP.
The sequence of events for this particular issue is like this: **At runtime:** - IEATDUMP is issued.
- A TQE that is used by the dumping process expires *before* the dump is complete (because we have a lot of private storage to dump in this case, and it simply takes a long wallclock time to complete).
- The TCBs in the dumped address space are forced to be MVS dispatchable again, so they may run before the dump completes.
- The IEATDUMP process finally ends and a complete dump is written. Because we know that we forced the TCBs to be dispatchable, and they could have run, and could have mutated storage we are interested in, the IEATDUMP service ends with the Rc2, Reas4, which tells is that "Data in the dump may be inconsistent'
 **After runtime, during diagnosis, using the IEATDUMP**
- Any code that uses the DTFJ API (e.g. jdpmview, MAT, service store, polyxena) to open this dump loops in com/ibm/j9ddr/corereaders/tdump/zebedee/le/DsaStackFrame.findSfxm
- This is probably because the TCB/pthread being looked at was inflight after being redispatched by MVS after the TQE expiry, so the expected 'frozen in time' stack frame data is now not walkable without this infinite loop in the diagnostic code. We are requesting for a fix to the j9ddr corereader code that will tolerate gracefully the state of the native stack found for that thread in the dump, or provide some kind of adhoc patch to the dump itself that will allow the dump to be initialized by tools that use DTFJ.

Java -version output
java version "11.0.14.1" 2022-02-08

Eclipse OpenJ9 VM 11.0.14.1 (build openj9-0.30.1, JRE 11 AIX ppc64-64-Bit Compressed References 20220215_254 (JIT enabled, AOT enabled)
OpenJ9 - 9dccbe076
OMR - 56c3376ba
JCL - f0981daedc based on jdk-11.0.14.1+1)
Summary of problem
On AIX 7.2(.5.3), after installing zlib library version 1.2.12 from OpenSource Toolbox, the extraction of a particular zip file with a simple Java program fails with following error:
invalid entry CRC (expected <hex> but got <hex>)[Ljava.lang.StackTraceElement;@5470688f
The same worked fine with the former zlib library version 1.2.11. Because the failure does not happen with any zip file, I can provide a simple reproducer kit on request.
The following facts have been figured out:
Semeru JDK11 loads the libz.a dynamically via LIBPATH, while the linked in default prefers the path /opt/freeware/lib to /lib:/usr/lib.
 The following command shows the actual path to libz.a, which is used in the current environment (Example for 'unset LIBPATH'):
 $ ldd java
 java needs:
 /opt/freeware/lib/libz.a(libz.so.1) <<<<<<< default location
 /usr/lib/libpthreads.a(shr_xpg5_64.o)
 /usr/lib/libc.a(shr_64.o)
 /unix
 /usr/lib/libcrypt.a(shr_64.o)
There may exist several different versions of libz.a on AIX at the same time and the LIBPATH variable determines which one is actually getting linked.
 $ rpm -q zlib (or: yum list installed|grep zlib)
 zlib-1.2.12-1.ppc <<<< /opt/freeware/bin/libz.a has v1.2.12-1
 $ ls /usr/lib/libz.a <<<< /usr/lib/libz.a has v1.2.11
 /usr/lib/libz.a
 $ ls -l /usr/lib/libz.a
 lrwxrwxrwx 1 root system 23 Apr 06 09:15 /usr/lib/libz.a -> /usr/opt/rpm/lib/libz.a
 $ lslpp -w /usr/opt/rpm/lib/libz.a
 File Fileset Type
 /usr/opt/rpm/lib/libz.a rpm.rte File
The same java example program works fine, if LIBPATH is set to a libz.a v1.2.11, but
 it fails, if LIBPATH is set to a libz.a v1.2.12-1 (which is currently the latest on AIX Toolbox for Open Source Software).
 So any customer can run into this on AIX 7, with the default condition (Semeru Java 11, unset LIBPATH, 'yum update' to latest).
The same reproducer example program works fine with Adoptium JDK 11 under the same conditions, so this seems to be specific to Semeru Java.

issue_title: Switch from using <init> to <new> for Value Types
description:
Currently JavaC compiles value classes with an `<init>` method instead of a `<new>` method. Because of this, class verification also assumes that value types will always use `<init>` and not `<new>`. When JavaC switches to using `<new>` instead of `<init>`, the verification code will have to switch as well.
#14816 has code to verify value types that have both `<init>` and `<new>` methods, but the code to verify the `<new>` methods is currently disabled. To enable it we just need to get rid of the `#if defined(J9VM_OPT_VALHALLA_NEW_FACTORY_METHOD)` checks, and then get rid of the code for verifying `<init>` (since it will no longer be relevant).

issue_title: Latest openJ9 JDK11 loads a class from wrong location on modular run
description:
Java -version output
openjdk version "11.0.15" 2022-04-19
IBM Semeru Runtime Open Edition 11.0.15.0 (build 11.0.15+10)
Eclipse OpenJ9 VM 11.0.15.0 (build openj9-0.32.0, JRE 11 Windows 10 amd64-64-Bit Compressed References 20220422_352 (JIT enabled, AOT enabled)
OpenJ9 - 9a84ec34e
OMR - ab24b6666
JCL - b7b5b42ea6 based on jdk-11.0.15+10)
Does not matter if windows or linux.
Summary of problem
I noticed a bug/issue on the latest OpenJDK 11.0.15+10 OpenJ9 0.32.0 (It was not there in the previous release, and not on the normal JDK11-s).
If I have an application with a custom classloader (I have given it null as the parent classloader) and try to load a class from it (that also exists in the normal classpath):
Class k = Class.forName("autotest.TargetUnver", true, new MyCustomClassLoader());
I will get on normal JDK and previous versions and current openJDK 11 with classpath run:
TargetUnver has classLoader autotest.MyCustomClassLoader@22a71081
But if I run the application as a modular application with module path, open latest openJDK 11 I will get:
TargetUnver has classLoader jdk.internal.loader.ClassLoaders$AppClassLoader@4418b527
This issue happens only in the latest OpenJDK11 with modular run.
Diagnostic files
I made a simple app to showcase the issue.
If you run it with classpath, all ok:
java -cp target\MyJar.jar autotest.Test
But the modular run gets a different result for some reason (does not happen on openJDK or older versions):
java --module-path target\MyJar.jar -m MyJar/autotest.Test
[simple-java-maven-app-master.zip](

With 17.0.2, class `C100` can be loaded, with 17.0.3 this triggers a `StackOverflowError`. On my machine 17.0.2. can still load `C375`. The highest class I can still load on 17.0.3 is `C75`. I tried setting `-Xss` but it does not seem to have any effect here.

 rec(n + 1);
}
But I did not notice much difference between 17.0.2 and 17.0.3 here. Again, setting `-Xss` does not seem to have an effect here.

issue_title: Incorrect return value when checking for Cyclical static VT field
description:
Noticed the following code that uses the return value of `checkForCyclicalVerification()` to set `cycleDetected` However, `checkForCyclicalVerification()` uses the return value of `verifyLoadingOrLinkingStack()`, which returns `FALSE` if circularity is detected.

issue_title: Support for encrypted performance metrics for JITServer
description:
JITServer can export internal performance metrics to a monitoring agent like Prometheus (#14762). At the moment these metrics are sent in plain text over the network. It would be best if we offer the user the possibility of encrypting this network traffic.
I am thinking that the options to encrypt performance metrics should be separate from the options to encrypt compilation requests and responses. That is, a user may elect to encrypt only the performance metrics or only the client-server communication.

issue_title: New DDR command `constantpool`
description:
Add a new DDR command for use in jdmpview that would print out the constantpool structure (ROM and RAM) for a given J9Class address.
format should be: `constantpool <ramclass>`
>!constantpool <hex>
Index ROM RAM Type Value
1 <hex> <hex> Fieldref [fieldNameAndSignature] #4,#8
2 !j9rommethod <hex> !j9method <hex> Methodref [methodNameAndSignature] #5,#9
3 !j9utf8 <hex> !j9object <hex> String [StringValue] #10
4 !j9romclass <hex> !j9class <hex> Class [className] #23
...
10 <hex> <hex> UTF8 TestString
For each parameter:
Index = index of the constantpool entry (this should start at 1 and up to romConstantpoolCount)
ROM = pointer to the object/struct address from `J9ROMConstantPoolItem` at index (obtained through j9class->ramConstantPool->romConstantPool[index])
RAM = pointer to the object/struct address from `J9RAMConstantPoolItem` at index (j9class->ramConstantPool[index])
Type = the constantpool entry type, this should be based on the bit flag from J9ROMCLASS_CPSHAPEDESCRIPTION(romClass)
Value = I suggest putting in the ROM values based on the entry Type, we could make this ROMValue and add a RAMValue to print the RAM value as well
for possible ConstantPool types: see Note: ROM constantpool can be larger than RAM constantpool so some entries will have no RAM address value
Note2: For entries in the ConstantPool that requires resolution (Class/Field/Method/MethodHandle/MethodType/String/ConstantDynamic), the ROM / RAM value may not be available if they have not been initialized/resolved, in such case, the ROM / RAM value should be NULL to reflect that state even if the target method/field/class already exist in memory

issue_title: "-Xdump:none" generates core files
description:
When OpenJ9 is running with `-Xdump:none`, it generates a system dump file (core file on Linux) if the VM crashes.
It is explained in as:
> If you remove all dump agents by using `-Xdump:none` with no further `-Xdump` options, the VM still provides these basic diagnostic outputs:
> - If a crash occurs, information about the location of the crash, VM options, and native and Java stack traces are written to stderr. **A system dump file is also written** to the user's home directory.
However, it is counterintuitive.
Specifying `-Xdump:system:none` turns off system dumps, then it is natural to expect `-Xdump:none` to turn off all the dumps (java, heap, jit, snap, system).
You can use the environment variable `J9NO_DUMPS` with `-Xdump:none` to stop system dumps. But that is not documented, and it has been malfunctioning until fixed by PR #15122.
I would propose `-Xdump:none` to stop generating core files by default.

issue_title: Install XCode / clang 12.4 to support Java 17+
description:
As per 11.2 with XCode / clang 12.4 is the supported compiler for Java 17+. OpenJ9 is currently documented as using 10.14 with xcode 10.3 and clang 10.0.1 for all versions.
I have 12.4 working with my internal systems after was merged.
As discovered working though this on my internal system, the minimum platform for jdk17+ should be 10.15 which also happens to be the minimum level xcode v12.4 will work on. This means that OpenJ9 system(s) need to upgraded first. Side note JDK8 & JDK11 will also build on 12.4 so we could keep the setup/configuration minimal by keeping the same version of xcode across all releases.

description:
Depends on When a Virtual thread enters a synch block (or method) it is pinned until it exits. Likewise for native functions and Object.wait().
Part 1: Basic Pinning support
- JNI callout increment counter, decrement when callout frame is popped
- monenter increment counter, vice versa on monexit (same for sync methods)
- Object.wait inc counter on entry, vice versa on exit
Part 2: Exception Throws
On exception throw, - track all frames that need to dec/inc the pin state counter as well
- real exception throws in JIT code handled by VM runtime helpers

issue_title: Loom: GC Thread scanning
description:
Depends on Threads should be scanned as they normally would. If a thread is mounted with a VirtualThread, then the virtual thread stack will be scanned, the carrier thread stack will be stored in a continuation instance.
All continuation objects will have a stack that can be found with the vmref field. These stacks should be scanned just as a regular platform thread would be.
We also need to consider concurrent aspects in regards to scanning. What happens if the GC is doing a concurrent scan and the VirtualThread attempts to mount/unmount? Perhaps we need a mechanism to block a mount/unmount operation while a thread stack is being scanned.

issue_title: Loom: GC collection of Continuations
description:
Depends on Virtual threads are not part of the root set. They are only alive if they are mounted on a carrier thread or if there is a strong reference to them (ie scheduler, blocking queue, etc.)
In order to determine which Continuations are dead
- when scanning Continuation remove from live continuation list and add to new continuation survivor list
- at the end of GC all continuations remaining in live continuation list can be cleaned up (recycled or freed)
 - for now we will just free them - continuation that survive make up new live continuation list after GC
GC will need a field on J9VMContinuation that it can use to create a linked list (similar `gcLink` in finalizable lists).

issue_title: Loom: Investigate solutions for <4gb memory limitations
description:
Depends on In the basic implementation all Continuation stacks are allocated in <4gb. This imposes a restriction on the number of active Continuations that we can have. The following solutions can address this.
Potential solution:
When creating a continuation, nothing changes, simply allocate the <4gb stack.
Upon yield, allocate a new >4gb memory region that is equivalent to the size of the continuation stack (this can be a new allocation or from freelist). Copy the continuation stack to the newly allocated stack on a yield and free the <4gb stack (the original stack). "copy" actually involves doing a stackwalk, similar to stack growing, to update all slots and account for stack allocated objects.
Upon entry to continuation get a new <4bg stack (this will be from free list) and copy the unmounted (>4gb) continuation stack contents to the new stack.
With this approach the GC still needs to know about Continuation objects, because it needs to walk their stacks. So essentially, from a GC perspective nothing changes from the basic implementation.
The benefits are that we the number of <4gb stacks for VirtualThreads is equivalent to the number of carrier threads *2 (one for a mounted Vthread, one for the carrier), so we can allocate a large number of VirtualThreads without issues. The memory allocations on entry and yield can be avoided by keeping a freelist of stacks. In fact we can pre-allocate all the <4gb stacks up front since that is a fixed number. We could potentially extend this approach to do a lazy copy when mounting a virtualthread, so not all frames are copied all at once, just the top most.

issue_title: Redesign of Locked Synchronizer processing
description:
JVM is supposed to respond to API where the list of threads and their Locked (Ownable) Synchronizes are provided:
We currently maintain the list of all live Synchronziers - every time we create an instance of such object we add it to the list (JIT is supposed to invoke a callback that will enqueue the object)
- at STW GCs and in Concurrent Scavenger we reset the list content and rebuild it. We recognize type of objects while traversing object graph, and at the point we add it to the new list. - for Concurrent Marking GC we use 'weak root' approach. We don't reset the list at GC start, but we prune the existing list at the end of GC cycle. We iterate the list and remove all those that did not survive.
The upside of this approach is that the list is readily available (except for CS case, if invoked in a middle of a cycle, when we are forced to finish the cycle first, before returning), but:
- the code is somewhat complex, spread out in 10s of files, and occasionally we get confusing bugs due to unusual list organization (without going into details why, it does not terminate with null, but with a value pointing back to the last item in the list)
- for Concurrent Marking case, the prunning pass can take a few milisec (an example provided below with ~9ms)

The new approach would be passive - on demand. We would walk the heap and recognize such objects and add them to the list. While believe that walking the heap at random point of time should not be an issue (class pointer even for unloaded classes is valid for some time, until we kill class segments, but if that occurs, we convert dead objects to holes), we realize that the content of dead objects found during the walk is stale. Since the API requires to associate Synchornizers with owning threads, we have to match the owner thread info from the synchronizer object with the list of currently live threads. In unlikely case that the object is dead and happened to have a dead thread owner matching a current live thread with the same id, we would incorrectly report a dead object.
So, to be just completely safe, we will rebuild the liveness information by performing GC, before actually doing the heap walk. Probably the simplest approach is to do it the same way how we deal with JVMTI APIs - we envoke ensureHeapWalkable, what not only rebuilds liveness info, but also removes all dead objects (makes holes out of them). While this approach will remove the downsides of current approach, clearly it will be way slower to respond to the API. The documentation however warns that APIs could be slow, and not given guidelines how quickly we should respond:
This method is designed for troubleshooting use, but not for synchronization control. It might be an expensive operation.

Bug Title: Redesign of Locked Synchronizer processing
Bug Description: JVM is supposed to respond to API where the list of threads and their Locked (Ownable) Synchronizes are provided:
We currently maintain the list of all live Synchronziers - every time we create an instance of such object we add it to the list (JIT is supposed to invoke a callback that will enqueue the object)
- at STW GCs and in Concurrent Scavenger we reset the list content and rebuild it. We recognize type of objects while traversing object graph, and at the point we add it to the new list. - for Concurrent Marking GC we use 'weak root' approach. We don't reset the list at GC start, but we prune the existing list at the end of GC cycle. We iterate the list and remove all those that did not survive.
The upside of this approach is that the list is readily available (except for CS case, if invoked in a middle of a cycle, when we are forced to finish the cycle first, before returning), but:
- the code is somewhat complex, spread out in 10s of files, and occasionally we get confusing bugs due to unusual list organization (without going into details why, it does not terminate with null, but with a value pointing back to the last item in the list)
- for Concurrent Marking case, the prunning pass can take a few milisec (an example provided below with ~9ms)

issue_title: CRIU: Better deadlock handling in core JDK code
description:
There are cases where the thread running a checkpoint requires access to a resource that is held by a halted thread. This will result in a deadlock. In some cases the relevant code is in the JDK so a user will not having any control of the issue. An example is the MethodType table lock which is essential when resolving a MethodHandle.
To solve this problem a new annotation will be introduced `@NotCheckpointSafe`
This annotation will be added to any internal API where a thread may be holding on to an essential resource. During checkpoint any thread with that annotation will not be halted immediately. Instead it will poll the thread and wait for that frame to be popped.
When no threads have the `@NotCheckpointSafe` annotation in any of their frames then the checkpoint will proceed.
creator: tajila
text:
Bug Title: CRIU: Better deadlock handling in core JDK code
Bug Description: There are cases where the thread running a checkpoint requires access to a resource that is held by a halted thread. This will result in a deadlock. In some cases the relevant code is in the JDK so a user will not having any control of the issue. An example is the MethodType table lock which is essential when resolving a MethodHandle.
To solve this problem a new annotation will be introduced `@NotCheckpointSafe`
This annotation will be added to any internal API where a thread may be holding on to an essential resource. During checkpoint any thread with that annotation will not be halted immediately. Instead it will poll the thread and wait for that frame to be popped.
When no threads have the `@NotCheckpointSafe` annotation in any of their frames then the checkpoint will proceed.

issue_title: JITServer compilation failures due to interrupted network I/O system calls
description: Network I/O system calls in JITServer communication layer can sometimes fail with the `EINTR` error (interrupted system call). Such failures at the JIT client can lead to failed remote compilations and are handled as a "lost connection", leading to subsequent compilations being performed locally for a short time period, which can result in memory usage spikes. JITServer networking code (including encrypted communication with SSL) needs to handle the `EINTR` errors that are possible during normal operation.

issue_title: JITServer compilation failures when using encryption
description:
Using JITServer with encryption can result in intermittent remote compilation failures with the error code `compilationStreamFailure` that are caused by SSL I/O errors. The main issue is that such failures are handled by the client as a lost connection, and compilations are performed locally at the client for a short period of time, which leads to memory usage spikes (that are supposed to be eliminated when using JITServer). This happens during normal operation, without any actual network errors.
With the default settings, the client resumes remote compilations 1 second after "losing" the connection, which results in dozens to hundreds of compilations performed locally. If the client is forced to reconnect immediately (using the `-Xjit:reconnectWaitTimeMs=0` option plus the fix in #15391), all compilations are performed remotely - the failed ones are immediately retried remotely and succeed. Increasing the client and server socket timeouts makes no difference.
Here are the SSL errors that I've seen printed to `stderr`, sorted from most to least frequent:
- at the client:
error:140943FC:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert bad record mac:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1528:SSL alert number 20
error:140943F2:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert unexpected message:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1528:SSL alert number 10
error:140940F4:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:unexpected message:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1461:
- at the server:
error:1408F119:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:decryption failed or bad record mac:../ssl/record/ssl3_record.c:677:
error:140E0197:SSL routines:SSL_shutdown:shutdown while in init:../ssl/ssl_lib.c:2078:
error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number:../ssl/record/ssl3_record.c:355:
error:140940F4:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:unexpected message:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1461:
Not all occurrences of `compilationStreamFailure` at the client have a matching SSL error printed to `stderr`.
The issue is reliably reproducible for me with AcmeAir+JMeter with multiple clients (e.g. 16), even when the server and the clients run on the same machine. I'm using Ubuntu 18.04 with OpenSSL 1.1.1. The issue is reproducible even with a single client compilation thread (although less frequently), thus this is probably not a multithreading issue.
Correctly closing the SSL connections (#15392) seems to get rid of the errors printed to `stderr` and makes the issue less frequent, but doesn't fix it completely. One possibility is that failed `BIO_read()` and `BIO_write()` calls need to be retried in some cases when indicated by `BIO_should_retry()` (similar to how it's done in #15217). Also see #15394.

issue_title: Invalid error message printed at JITServer start with custom number of threads
description:
If the number of JITServer compilation threads is customized using the `-XcompilationThreads<N>` option, an invalid error message is printed to `stderr` when JITServer starts:
Requested number of compilation threads is over the limit of 15. Will use 15 threads.
However, the number of threads is set correctly.
It looks like the `-XcompilationThreads` option is first parsed before JITServer options are parsed, which results in the option being rejected because the number of threads is larger than the JIT client limit (15), and later parsed again and handled correctly.

issue_title: Add options to bypass JITServer AOT cache per method
description: As a debugging/diagnostic feature, we should to have a way of bypassing the JITServer AOT cache on a per method basis, similar to excluding methods from JIT or AOT compilation/load. This can be useful, e.g., to determine whether a problem with a given method is caused by an AOT compiler issue or an AOT cache method serialization/deserialization issue. For completeness, there should be two separate options to forbid storing and loading a method to/from the JITServer AOT cache, e.g. `-Xaot:{method}(jitserverAOTCacheNoStore)` and `-Xaot:{method}(jitserverAOTCacheNoLoad)`. These options should be specified on the client side.

issue_title: CRIU: Address System.nanoTime deficiencies when machine reboots
description:
The existing solution to fixup System.nanoTime involves getting the nanotime pre and post checkpoint to compute the "JVMdowntime" delta. This approach assumes that the nanoTime clock has the same time base pre and post checkpoint. We have noticed that rebooting the machine resets the timebase.
We will fix this issue by using nano wall clock time to determine the "JVMdowntime" (`InternalCRIUSupport.getCheckpointRestoreNanoTimeDelta`). For System.nanoTime, instead of returning `nanoTime - JVMdowntime` it will instead return `nanoTime - PrePostCheckpointNanottimeClockDelta`.
The `PrePostCheckpointNanottimeClockDelta` is essentially the difference between the nanotime clock in checkpoint and restore.

issue_title: Customers do not like that the Attach API is enabled by default on Windows, AIX, and Linux.
description:
Customers do not like that the Attach API is enabled by default on Windows, AIX, and Linux.
(The Attach API is not enabled by default on z/OS.)
The customer doesn't like that /tmp/.com_ibm_tools_attach create files with world writeable files.
The customer provided this feedback:
"Our GIS team is asking if there is no legitimate use for this without the AttachAPI usage, then why is it being enabled by default at all?
As long as these files are being created by any Java command or process, there will be the perception that they will be vulnerable to attacks such as these without very detailed monitoring in place to look for more than the empty control files.
Why put all of these teams through getting some monitoring solution in place when this can just be disabled by default and development teams can enable it easy enough as it is needed?"
This customer is on Linux with 1000's of Java processes spread over 100s of hosts and to completely disable the Attach API, they have to add -Dcom.ibm.tools.attach.enable=no to the two options.default files every time they install Java or upgrade Java.

issue_title: Loom: Add support for direct transition to interpreter on continuation entry
description:
The current implementation creates a new interpreter instance on continuation entry (resuming or a creating a new one). This is going to eat up stack space.
To address this, a new callin helper will be added to (`setupRunStaticMethod`) which resolves the method (and init class), builds a frame and sets up the args but doesnt instanstiate a new interpreter.
THe continuation enter code will be amend to transition back to the interpreter with the new interpreter variables rather than creating a new instance

issue_title: Loom: Investigate alternate JIT register spilling
description:
See The issue here is that the a continuation can be run in two ways - the initial mount onto a carrier thread and a remount at some point after the continuation yields (possibly on a different carrier thread).
When run for the first time, a call-in results in a new ELS being created on the C stack of the carrier thread. When a continuation is remounted, the goal is not to call-in.
The JIT spilled registers are currently stored in the C interpreter native stack frame (ELS points to these locations on the C stack). For the initial run, the registers are stored in the call-in stack frame like any other thread. When the continuation is remounted, that ELS will not exist.
creator: gacholio

issue_title: CRIU: delay interrupt requests to hatled threads
description: In single thread mode sending an interrupt request to a halted (halted by wait) thread in a synchronized block will cause the thread to acquire the resource thus potentially causing a deadlock. To solve this we can reuse the delay notification event logic to delay the notification request.
creator: tajila
text:
Bug Title: CRIU: delay interrupt requests to hatled threads
Bug Description: In single thread mode sending an interrupt request to a halted (halted by wait) thread in a synchronized block will cause the thread to acquire the resource thus potentially causing a deadlock. To solve this we can reuse the delay notification event logic to delay the notification request.

Summary of problem
Javacore generation with kill -3 completely freezes JVM on 8.0.7.10 onwards for process with high number of threads
The HMC Next product moved from 8.0.7.6 to 8.0.7.10 and this problem started. In the product test environment, every time a javacore is generated using kill -3, the Java process completely hangs, and absolutely no response or movement within the JVM. The change which introduced the issue is : Next steps
As the Issue is on high priority and as the hang occurs during javacore generation which is the basic functionality we expect getting more similar issues from other customers as well starting from Java 8.0.7.10.
@tajila @pshipton Could you please consider providing a command line option so that the resolving of function name can be disabled/enabled?
From service perspective, this new option is needed because :
1. Resolving the function names at least are time consuming and could be problematic (just like this current issue).
2. Most customers do not care about the function names in the native stack trace
3. We only care about the native stack trace function names to resolve crash issues and hangs in native stack traces.
4. We have the nativeDecoder to get the information from the generated javacore file or native stderr messages.
5. We can use gdb/gcore to obtain the information if necessary.
6. We do not have this information in Javacore files for so many years. Thanks in Advance for all your help on this issue!

issue_title: Concurrent Scavenger might have incorrect settings for GS support
description:
Concurrent Scavenger might have incorrect settings for GS support on machines with Guarded Storage HW (z14+) available if Concurrent Scavenger is used with `J9_EXTENDED_RUNTIME2_ENABLE_PORTABLE_SHARED_CACHE` mode or CRIU support.
GC expects usage `softwareRangeCheckReadBarrier` but JIT attempts to use HW.
It might lead to GC assert with the message "readObject ... in Evacuate".
The workaround is adding `-XXgc:softwareRangeCheckReadBarrier` option.
creator: dmitripivkine

java -jar ./junit-platform-console-standalone-1.8.2.jar -cp ./test-classes:./classes:./guava-31.0.1-jre.jar:./javax.inject-1.jar:./failureaccess-1.0.1.jar -m com.google.inject.spi.InjectionPointTest#testConstructorInjectionPoint

issue_title: Add options to control resolution of native stack symbols
description:
With eclipse/omr#6345, more native stack symbols are resolved. However, if an application has a large number of threads, the additional cost of that work can mean that producing a java dump takes longer than the code is prepared for leading to an incomplete dump, or in some cases a hanging process.
For that reason, the default behavior was changed with eclipse-openj9/openj9#15659 to use the options introduced in eclipse/omr#6629 to request full symbol resolution only for a thread responding to a signal (perhaps a fault).
A user might prefer to have that improved symbol resolution, despite those possibilities. This proposes that new command-line options be introduced.
* `-XX:-ShowNativeStackSymbols` - don't show any native stack symbols (not even in response to a signal)
* `-XX:+ShowNativeStackSymbols=basic` - show only easily acquired native stack symbols
* `-XX:+ShowNativeStackSymbols=all` - show all available native stack symbols

issue_title: Loom: Move unmounted continuation stacks out of the low memory area
description:
If running compressed references, when a continuation stack is unmounted, it should be copied into new memory not allocated in the <4Gb area. When remounted, copy the stack back to the low memory area.
The complication is stack-allocated objects which point to other stack-allocated objects. Because the reference slots in the objects are only 32 bits wide, they can't simply be relocated.

issue_title: DTFJ Javacore parser is missing stack traces etc. with current Javacore files
description:
The DTFJ Javacore parser is meant to extract information from the javacore.xxxx.txt file generated by the JVM.
It works, but not as well as it used to as it does not extract Java and native stack traces from the javacore file.
This is probably because the javacore file format has been enhanced with additional information, but this confuses the parser. Removing some of the extra lines from the javacore file lets DTFJ extract more information. The DTFJ parser should be improved to ignore those extra lines, or better still, make any additional information be available from DTFJ, while still being able to parse javacore files from older JVMs.

issue_title: [JDK19] JVMTI VirtualThread[Mount|UnMount] Events
description:
**JVMTI VirtualThreadMount and VirtualThreadUnMount events** are part of the **JVMTI Extension API**, which is not covered by the [JVMTI documentation]( So, they don't need to be supported for the current [Java 19 milestone](
Their implementation will be similar to the VirtualThreadStart and VirtualThreadEnd events. VirtualThreadStart and VirtualThreadEnd events are only triggered during the first mount and last unmount respectively. But, VirtualThreadMount and VirtualThreadUnMount events will be triggered on each mount and unmount respectively.
The following **JVMTI serviceability tests will need to be disabled** until support for the VirtualThreadMount and VirtualThreadUnMount events is introduced:
vthread/BreakpointInYieldTest/libBreakpointInYieldTest.cpp
vthread/MethodExitTest/libMethodExitTest.cpp
vthread/NullAsCurrentThreadTest/libNullAsCurrentThreadTest.cpp
vthread/VThreadTest/libVThreadTest.cpp
vthread/VThreadUnsupportedTest/libVThreadUnsupportedTest.cpp

issue_title: [JDK19] JVMTI GetVirtualThread
description:
JVMTI **GetVirtualThread** is part of the JVMTI Extension API, which is not covered by the [JVMTI documentation]( So, it doesn't need to be supported for the current [Java 19 milestone](
GetVirtualThread just returns the virtual thread object corresponding to a carrier thread via one of the input parameters. It's the inverse of GetCarrierThread (see The following **JVMTI serviceability tests will need to be disabled** until support for GetVirtualThread is introduced:

issue_title: [JDK19] JVMTI framepop02.java#id1 and singlestep01 Segfault
description:
`framepop02/framepop02.java#id1` and `SingleStep/singlestep01` pass with the RI. These tests are related to Project Loom. The test failures will only be seen in JDK19+.
Related: #16187.
 Issue
There is a recursive infinite loop. The test registers a JVMTI event callback for `MethodEntry`, and invokes `jvmtiGetThreadInfo` from the `MethodEntry` event callback. `jvmtiGetThreadInfo` loads the `java/lang/Thread$Constants` class for the virtual thread path. While loading this class, the `MethodEntry` event callback is invoked again. Then, we are stuck in an infinite loop: `MethodEntry` event callback -> `jvmtiGetThreadInfo` -> `MethodEntry` event callback -> `jvmtiGetThreadInfo`.
A similar recursive infinite loop is seen in `SingleStep/singlestep01`: `SingleStep` event callback -> `jvmtiGetThreadInfo` -> `SingleStep` event callback -> `jvmtiGetThreadInfo`.
To resolve this issue, I tried adding `java/lang/Thread$Constants` to the `requiredClasses` array in `jclcinit.c`. But `java/lang/Thread$Constants` has a static init block which fails to successfully execute at startup: [Thread.java#L3037-L3065](

issue_title: [JDK19] JVMTI ContFramePopTest Fails
description:
`vthread/ContFramePopTest` passes with the RI. This test is related to Project Loom and will only be seen with JDK19+.
Related: #16187.
 Issue
Currently, OpenJ9 assumes `J9VMThread->currentContinuation` to be NULL if a platform thread is runnning. In other words, we expect a non-null `J9VMThread->currentContinuation` only when `J9VMThread->threadObject` is an instance of virtual thread. A non-null `J9VMThread->currentContinuation` signifies a mounted virtual thread. In JVMTI, this is used as an indicator to swap stacks when `jvmtiNotifyFramePop` is invoked on a platform thread. This test runs a continuation directly on a platform thread and violates the assumption related to `J9VMThread->currentContinuation`. `J9VMThread->currentContinuation` is non-null when a virtual thread is not mounted. This leads to an incorrect decision to swap stack, which causes the test to fail.
 Test CMD
make test TEST="jtreg:test/hotspot/jtreg/serviceability/jvmti/vthread/ContFramePopTest/ContFramePopTest.java" JTREG="JAVA_OPTIONSenable-preview -Dvm.continuations=true;VERBOSE=all"
 Test Output
STDOUT:
Agent_OnLoad started
Agent_OnLoad finished
 main: started enableEvents: started
enableEvents: finished
 runTest: started ## runTest: iteration #0
## cont: started ##
 cont: iteration #0
<<<< runTest: before foo(): 3, abc, 0.0 <<<<
 foo: started foo: before bar(): 8, yyy, 1
MethodEntry event #1: thread: MainThread, method: ContFramePopTest: zzz()Ljava/lang/String;
MethodEntry: Requesting FramePop notifications for top frame
check_jvmti_status: JVMTI function returned error: JVMTI_ERROR_OPAQUE_FRAME (32)
STDERR:
Fatal error: MethodEntry: error in JVMTI NotifyFramePop

issue_title: JEP 434: Foreign Function & Memory API (Second Preview)
description:
See for JDK20 with the following changes in terms of APIs which affects our FFI implementation in Java.
This JEP proposes to incorporate refinements based on feedback, and to re-preview the API in JDK 20. In this version:
1. The MemorySegment and MemoryAddress abstractions are unified
 (memory addresses are now modeled by zero-length memory segments), and
2. The sealed MemoryLayout hierarchy is enhanced to facilitate usage with pattern matching in switch expressions and statements ([JEP 427](

issue_title: JVMTI framepop02.java#id1 checks outside a virtual thread's scope
description:
Issue
In `framepop02/framepop02.java#id1`, the JVMTI frame pop event expects the thread to be a virtual thread after the invocation of `VirtualThread.unmount`.
This is not true since `J9VMThread->threadObject` is changed to the carrier thread in `VirtualThread.unmount`.
Virtual thread's scope is between the `mount` and `unmount` phases. The test should enforce its checks within a virtual thread's scope.
Currently, this test is incompatible with OpenJ9 since it enforces its checks outside a virtual thread's scope.

issue_title: Path to openjdk reference repo doesn't work on Windows
description:
**Describe the bug**
I noticed the following when running a grinder on Windows (because Windows was quite a bit slower than other platforms).
 [exec] git clone --depth 1 -q --reference-if-able C:\cygwin64\home\jenkins/openjdk_cache openjdk-jdk
 [exec] info: Could not add alternate for 'C:cygwin64homejenkins/openjdk_cache': path 'C:cygwin64homejenkins/openjdk_cache' does not exist
**To Reproduce**
Run a grinder on the OpenJ9 jenkins on an openjdk test.
**Expected behavior**
The path should be specified such that the reference repo is resolved.
@AdamBrousseau

issue_title: Value Types: AOT compilation mistakenly consider java/lang/Object as not VT in objectInequalityComparison transformation
description:
I noticed an error with AOT compilation of `java/lang/Object.equals(Ljava/lang/Object;)Z` when VT is enabled and SVM is not used. [aotlog.7500.37154.20221214.085914.7500.txt](
AOT: isValue: return isValueTypeClass 0 clazz <hex> Ljava/lang/Object;
Because `isValue` thinks `java/lang/Object` is NOT a value type,`objectInequalityComparison` ends up being transformed into `acmpne`, which is wrong if the instance is indeed VT. The reason is that when it checks if it's a fixed class, it calls `getObjectClassPointer` first [1]. When it is AOT compilation and SVM is not used, `getObjectClassPointer` returns `NULL` [2]. We end up calling `isValueTypeClass` on `java/lang/Object` at the end [3] and returns `TR_no`. I think one possible fix is to call `isJavaLangObject` on the `type` to check if it is `java/lang/Object` and return `TR_maybe` if yes.

issue_title: The number of Thread instance names starts with 3
description:

public class MyJVMTest {
 public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
 Runnable runnable = () -> {};
 Thread thread = new Thread(runnable);

issue_title: MaxDirectMemorySize memory size reported by -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal is incorrect (i.e it's -1 by default)
description:
Elasticsearch uses few math formulas for basic JVM ergonomics when launching without explicit heap size settings. We look at the max available heap and the max direct memory on the system, and then we use them to determine what's a good heap size for the JVM.
Running the following command below produces this output with j9:
bash
java -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal
[Global flags]
 size_t MaxHeapSize = 16828923904 {product} {ergonomic}
 uint64_t MaxDirectMemorySize = 18446744073709551615 {product} {ergonomic}
Running Hotspot with the same produces:
bash
 size_t MaxHeapSize = 16835936256 {product} {ergonomic}
 uint64_t MaxDirectMemorySize = 0 {product} {default}
According to the Java SE docs, it should be 0 if it's not specified:
Sets the maximum total size (in bytes) of the New I/O (the java.nio package) direct-buffer allocations. Append the letter k or K to indicate kilobytes, m or M to indicate megabytes, g or G to indicate gigabytes. **By default, the size is set to 0,** meaning that the JVM chooses the size for NIO direct-buffer allocations automatically.
 (search for `XX:MaxDirectMemorySize`)

issue_title: [FFI] Handling the captured exception or invalid values from the upcall method
description:
There is a leftover issue with the captured exception/invalid value (e.g. null or heap segment for struct) returned from the upcall method which was inappropriately handled in the existing FFI implementation. To be specific, the exception captured in the upcall method is passed back to the native function in downcall from the dispatcher, which leads to unexpected behavior (e.g. crash when casting the invalid return value in the native function). Such illegal situations include but is no limited to the following cases:
1. throw an exception from the upcall method
2. return `MemorySegment.NULL` (a native segement with a zero address) from the upcall method
3. return return `null` for struct from the upcall method
4. return a heap segment for struct from the upcall method
5. return a heap segment for pointer (the native address) which is not allowed as the native address of heap segment is set to zero by default.
For case 1, we propose to exploit `setjump/longjmp` to skip over the native function in downcall from the dispatcher to the call-out frame to guarantee the excepted exception is correctly thrown out. For case 2-5, the returned value will be handled by a call-in at first from the dispatcher where the exception is captured in the case of invalid value, in which case it should be handled in the same way as case 1.
Note:
1) the proposal is not specific to the FFI implementation in JDK20 but all java versions with the FFI support (JDK17+), in which case the final solution should work for JDK17/19/20+
2) the final solution will include the handling of the passed-in arguments in downcall as required in JDK20. 3) the changes will be made on the top of the current work in JDK20 to avoid any conflict in code.

issue_title: JVMTI suspend and resume rework to remove the virtual thread list
description:
This proposal updates the JVMTI suspend and resume mechanism for virtual threads so that it no longer has to rely on the virtual thread list. The end goal is to improve performance by removing the virtual thread list.
1. Declare a global variable in J9JavaVM: `allVirtualThreadsSuspended`.
2. In `jvmtiSuspendAllVirtualThreads`, set `allVirtualThreadsSuspended` to `TRUE`, and scan all carrier threads to suspend mounted virtual threads (similar to `jvmtiGetAllThreads`).
3. In `jvmtiResumeAllVirtualThreads`, set `allVirtualThreadsSuspended` to `FALSE`, and scan all carrier threads to resume mounted virtual threads (similar to `jvmtiGetAllThreads`).
4. In `JVM_VirtualThreadMountEnd`, set halt flag in the current `J9VMThread` if `allVirtualThreadsSuspended` is set to `TRUE`.
5. In `jvmtiResumeThread`, set `java.lang.VirtualThread.isSuspendedByJVMTI` to a specific value, which will allow to mount the thread, if `allVirtualThreadsSuspended` is set to `TRUE`. If the virtual thread is already mounted, only the halt flag needs to be cleared.
7. In `jvmtiSuspendThread`, reset `java.lang.VirtualThread.isSuspendedByJVMTI` if `allVirtualThreadsSuspended` is set to `TRUE`.
8. In `jvmtiGetThreadState`, inspect `allVirtualThreadsSuspended` and `java.lang.VirtualThread.isSuspendedByJVMTI` for setting the `SUSPEND` flag.

issue_title: Post-restore `-Xshareclasses` change semantics
description:
This issue tracks what changes can be made via the `-Xshareclasses` option post-restore. For 0.38, the plan is to introduce `-Xshareclasses:disableOnRestore` [1] which is a best effort implementation to disable the SCC, and can only be specified post restore [2].
Post 0.38, Some reasonable changes to support may be
* `-Xshareclasses:none` to `-Xshareclasses:...` and vice versa
* Adding `verbose` post-restore
* Modifying sizes via the `-Xsc*` variants
## VM Changes
TBD
## JIT Changes
Most changes to `-Xshareclasses`/`-Xsc*` don't impact the JIT as all interactions with the SCC are done via APIs. Adding `-Xshareclasses:none` post-restore is trivial to implement (it is essentially the same work needed to implement `-Xshareclasses:disableOnRestore`); doing the opposite will be more work and boils down to implementing <hr/>
[1] [2]

issue_title: Dockerfiles should specify non-root USER
description:
One of the IBM scans flagged 3 Dockerfiles for not using a non-root USER
buildenv\docker\aarch64-linux_CC\Dockerfile
buildenv\docker\armhf-linux_CC\Dockerfile
buildenv\docker\test\Dockerfile
We may have the same issue with mkdocker.sh. I see the USER being created but I don't see a line that switches to that user by the end of the Dockerfile.
>When executing a Docker image, by default the user that runs the process is root. As a best practice, you should run with a user that does not have high privileges; this help prevent privilege escalation. Apple the Principle of Least Privilege (POLP) when building or running a Docker image: give your user only the privileges it needs to perform the intended functions.
>
>To protect against privilege escalation, run with a user that only has enough privileges to perform the intended functions. You can use ROOT to configure your machine and install tools you need, mount driver, create new users and other function that require ROOT access. Then use the Docker USER command to define the user to run the image as. Use either: USER <user>[:<group>] or USER <UID>[:<GID>]

issue_title: Do not allocate/carve a new code cache if the JVM is low on physical memory
description:
Some JVMs run in containers with very low memory limits and using too much code cache can push them over the limits.
This issue proposes to read the available physical memory when a new code cache is allocated and proceed with the allocation only if the memory availability allows us to do so.
There are two situations to consider:
1) The JVM is using a code cache repository (256 MB) which is allocated up-front and individual code caches are carved from this repository. The JIT must prevent carving if the memory is very low. `carveCodeCacheSpaceFromRepository()` is the relevant routine.
2) The JVM does not use a code cache repository and memory for code caches is allocated on demand (2 MB). In this case, in theory, the allocation should fail if memory is not available, but I have read that Linux is optimistic with memory allocations and it "successfully" allocates memory even when there isn't any (failure will happen when touching an allocated page).
`TR::CompilationInfo::computeAndCacheFreePhysicalMemory(bool &incompleteInfo, int64_t updatePeriodMs)` can be used for reading available memory

issue_title: Timing hole between concurrent scanning and freeContinuation
description: For last unmounting continuation, the related J9VMContinuation structure need to be freed/recycled and reset vmref (point to the J9VMContinuation) in the contunuation Object, the related native memory might be reallocated for new continuation, currently we use the filed state of J9VMContinuation to avoid concurrent scan the finished continuation(after last unmounting), before checking J9VMContinuation->state, we need to verify the vmref is not NULL, but freeContinuation could happen in between, it would cause we retrieve incorrect J9VMContinuation->state and potentially cause JVM crash.

issue_title: Add support for -XX:+EnableDynamicAgentLoading
description:
Currently, j9 supports dynamic loading agents by default. The capabilities required for agents are: J9_EXTENDED_RUNTIME_OSR_SAFE_POINT
J9_EXTENDED_RUNTIME_ENABLE_HCR
These are currently enabled all the time. We need to put default enablement of these capabilities under the `EnableDynamicAgentLoading` flag. This will make it possible to turn off `EnableDynamicAgentLoading` in a future release if it is required in a future release. For now `EnableDynamicAgentLoading` can remain enabled by default. This will change likely in JDK21.
Additionally, we need to detect jvm agents attached are startup. We can look at `createAgentLibrary(` and lazily add the OSR/HCR flags when this occurs. We should add a runtime flag, for dynamic agent loading, this can be used to check if an agent is allowed to be loading at runtime.
The end result is:
1) When `EnableDynamicAgentLoading` is enabled, OSR/HCR flags are enable and dynamic agent loading is also enabled.
2) When `EnableDynamicAgentLoading` is disabled, OSR/HCR is only enabled when agents are attached at startup. Dynamic loading of agents is disabled.

description:

issue_title: New ImplicitCreation Attribute in project Valhalla
description:
New spec: The new `ImplicitCreation` Attribute in the class file needs to be consumed by OpenJ9. It has 2 attribute flags:
ACC_DEFAULT | <hex> | Allows use of the initial instance as a default value.
ACC_NON_ATOMIC | <hex> | Allows non-atomic updates to create new instances from the field values of existing instances.
We need J9Class flags to represent them. We may be able to reuse existing flag for `ACC_DEFAULT`.

issue_title: Improve DDR support for Continuation objects list
description:
Current implementation of Continuation objects list uses non-allocation caches in GC. This brings limitation full lists in DDR can be viewed in the case if core was generated with `(exclusive+prepwalk)` only.
We are planning to change implementation for Continuation objects list in the nearest future.
So, creating this item as a reminder that DDR code should be either redesigned (in the case of brand new solution) or improved (in the case non-allocation caches still be used).

issue_title: SPDX License Identifier in file headers is invalid
description:
I found the following `SPDX-License-Identifier` in your [template]( and at least some of the source files in this repository.
`EPL-2.0 OR Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0 WITH Classpath-exception-2.0 OR LicenseRef-GPL-2.0 WITH Assembly-exception`
The expression is not correct SPDX and so can't be processed correctly by an SPDX parser. The only serious problem is that `Assembly-exception` is not the correct identifier for the Assembly Exception. It should be `OpenJDK-assembly-exception-1.0`. Less serious, `GPL-2.0` is deprecated and `LicenseRef-GPL-2.0` is a form that you use when the license doesn't have an SPDX identifier; both of these should be `GPL-2.0-only`.
The actual expression should be something like this:
`EPL-2.0 OR Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only WITH Classpath-exception-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only WITH OpenJDK-assembly-exception-1.0`

issue_title: java -Xshareclasses -version fails with JVMSHRC829E if HOME is not set with Open 0.38.0
description:
I found a surprising difference between Java 17.0.6 (OpenJ9 0.36.0) and Java 17.0.7 (OpenJ9 0.38.0) in a startup shell trying to launch a Java process with -shared option and HOME environment variable being not set.
It looks likes a small regression, easy to by-pass (just export HOME=<any possible value>), but I'd be interested to get OpenJ9 developer's view on it.
I made a small case to reproduce it with this shell in /tmp/test.sh:
#!/bin/bash unset HOME java -Xshareclasses -version On acme1 machine (Linux CentOS 7.9 x64 with IBM Semeru JDK 17.0.6 installed), everything runs fine:
[root@acme1 ~]# /tmp/test.sh
openjdk version "17.0.6" 2023-01-17
IBM Semeru Runtime Open Edition 17.0.6.0 (build 17.0.6+10)
Eclipse OpenJ9 VM 17.0.6.0 (build openj9-0.36.0, JRE 17 Linux amd64-64-Bit Compressed References 20230117_397 (JIT enabled, AOT enabled)
OpenJ9 - e68fb241f
OMR - f491bbf6f
JCL - 927b34f84c8 based on jdk-17.0.6+10)
On acme2 machine (RockyLinux 8.7 x64, with IBM Semeru JDK 17.0.7 installed), the same sample shell fails:
[root@acme2 ~]# /tmp/test.sh JVMSHRC829E Failed to use user's home as the default shared cache directory. Cannot get home directory. Please set another directory via environment variable "HOME" or command line option "cacheDir=", or fix the home directory in the password file entry. JVMSHRC840E Failed to start up the shared cache. JVMJ9VM015W Initialization error for library j9shr29(11): JVMJ9VM009E J9VMDllMain failed Error: Could not create the Java Virtual Machine. Error: A fatal exception has occurred. Program will exit. Note, on acm2 machine, we have:
[root@acme2 ~]# java -version openjdk version "17.0.7" 2023-04-18 IBM Semeru Runtime Open Edition 17.0.7.0 (build 17.0.7+7) Eclipse OpenJ9 VM 17.0.7.0 (build openj9-0.38.0, JRE 17 Linux amd64-64-Bit Compressed References 20230418_480 (JIT enabled, AOT enabled) OpenJ9 - d57d05932 OMR - 855813495 JCL - 9d7a231edbc based on jdk-17.0.7+7) Any thought on why this need of HOME suddenly became mandatory ?
Thanks,
Alex

issue_title: JVMTI MethodExitTest test fails with JVMTI_ERROR_OPAQUE_FRAME error
description:
Issue
The test failed due to the NotifyFramePop of the breakpoint-1 function. After looking into the stack trace, it was discovered that the enterImpl()Z(enterContinuationImpl) method was being attempted to be popped by the NotifyFramePop, which results in the JVMTI_ERROR_OPAQUE_FRAME problem.
There are other NotifyFramePop calls in the test, which fail with the same error but at different methods:
- notifyJvmtiMountEnd
- notifyJvmtiUnmountEnd
**RI behavior:** The same functions in the RI are skipped or hidden during the NotifyFramePop. We can follow the same behavior as RI to fix the test. Any of the below approach can be used to fix the issue.
This means that the RI is ignoring/skipping/hidding methods that are involved to transition the context from a carrier thread to a virtual thread, and vice-versa. The context switch (internal) workings are being hidden from a Java user.
Context switch (internal) workings will also include the following methods:
- notifyJvmtiMountBegin
- notifyJvmtiUnmountBegin
- notifyJvmtiHideFrames
 There are three solutions:
- skip the impacted methods only in JVMTI;
- hide/ignore the impacted methods during stack walk everywhere; or
- don't match the RI since it is not defined in the specification, and exclude the test.

issue_title: Investigate perf impact of VirtualThread notifyJVMTI APIs
description:
notifyJvmtiMount
notifyJvmtiUnmount
These calls are used in every VirtualThread transition, #17372 added FastJNI support to reduce the need of transition from JIT to VM. As these are only useful for synchronization when a JVMTI agent is attached, VM should detect if such path are actually used and avoid calling such if possible.
As a prototype, we should detect if JVMTI agent is attached, or allowed to attach during runtime (`-XX:+EnableDynamicAgentLoading`). if neither apply, then VM should skip the execution of these code and directly return.
